content:
# llms.txt & AI Search Optimization: The 2026 Guide to Being Cited by ChatGPT and Gemini

Search is no longer just ten blue links. Google's AI Overviews now reach more than 2.5 billion users monthly across 200+ countries (Google I/O 2026), ChatGPT has surpassed 1.2 billion weekly users, and independent tracking puts AI-powered tools at roughly 12-15% of the global search market by the end of 2025 - roughly doubling within a year. When 58.5% of US Google searches ended without an external click in 2025, and that zero-click rate climbs to 83% when AI Overviews appear, the businesses that win are the ones AI models **cite**.

This guide explains AI search optimization (also called Generative Engine Optimization, or GEO): what llms.txt is, how it works alongside robots.txt and schema markup, and the practical steps ArtX recommends for making your brand machine-readable.

---

## Quick Answer: What Is AI Search Optimization (GEO)?

> **The Short Answer:** AI search optimization (GEO) is the practice of structuring your website's content so generative AI systems - ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews - can reliably understand, trust, and cite it in their answers. Key tactics include publishing a well-structured llms.txt file at your domain root, using factual plain-language content with clear headings, adding schema markup, and earning authoritative mentions, because AI engines synthesize answers from sources they can parse confidently rather than simply ranking pages.

Research makes the payoff concrete: AI-referred traffic converts at approximately 14.2% compared to roughly 2.8% for traditional Google organic traffic, and being cited in a Google AI Overview can lift your click-through rate by about 35% compared to not being cited (SEOmator, 2026). The traffic is smaller in volume but dramatically higher in intent. Read our broader outlook on [how AI search engines are reshaping SEO](/blog/future-of-seo-ai-search-engines) for the strategic context.

---

## What Is llms.txt and Why Does It Matter?

The **llms.txt** file is a proposed web standard (introduced by Jeremy Howard of Answer.ai in 2024) that gives large language models a concise, Markdown-formatted map of your site's most important content. Think of it as the AI-era sibling of `robots.txt`:

- **robots.txt** tells crawlers which pages they may access.
- **sitemap.xml** tells crawlers which pages exist and when they changed.
- **llms.txt** tells AI systems what your site is *about* in a format optimized for their context windows.

A standard llms.txt lives at `https://yourdomain.com/llms.txt` and contains an H1 with the site name, a blockquote summary, and categorized links to your key documentation, guides, and product pages. Many AI crawlers (notably from Perplexity and Anthropic) do consult it, though it is an emerging convention rather than a universally enforced standard - it works best as part of a broader machine-readability strategy.

### A Minimal llms.txt Example

```
# Acme Dental Care

> Affordable dental clinic in Dhanmondi, Dhaka. Services: implants, braces, root canals.

## Services
- [Dental Implants](/services/implants/): Permanent tooth replacement from 25,000 BDT
- [Orthodontics](/services/braces/): Braces and clear aligners for teens and adults

## Guides
- [Root Canal Cost in Bangladesh 2026](/blog/root-canal-cost-bangladesh/): Pricing, procedure, recovery
```

### How llms.txt Compares to Existing Standards

| Standard | Purpose | Audience | Status |
|----------|---------|----------|--------|
| robots.txt | Crawl permissions | Search crawlers | Universal, decades old |
| sitemap.xml | URL inventory | Search crawlers | Universal standard |
| Schema markup | Structured facts | Search engines + AI | Established, recommended by Google |
| llms.txt | Content summary in Markdown | AI models | Emerging proposal, growing adoption |

---

## How AI Engines Choose What to Cite

AI search systems do not rank pages the way classic search did. They retrieve a set of candidate sources, then synthesize an answer. Independent analysis shows AI engines frequently cite sources that are **not** the top conventional Google rankings - being understood matters as much as being ranked. The patterns researchers have observed:

### 1. Factual, Plainly Stated Claims Win

AI models extract assertions from your text. Pages written in clear, declarative sentences with named sources are easier to quote than pages wrapped in marketing fluff. Prefer "Our corporate websites launch in 4-6 weeks on average" over "We deliver solutions at the speed of thought."

### 2. Structure Is Machine-Readable Hierarchy

Descriptive H2/H3 headings, short paragraphs, tables, and FAQ sections map cleanly onto how AI systems segment content. A well-organized FAQ page is disproportionately likely to be cited because it mirrors the question-answer format these systems produce.

### 3. Authority Signals Still Count

Earning mentions from established publications, maintaining an accurate Google Business Profile, and accumulating genuine reviews feed the trust signals AI systems inherit from their training data and retrieval indexes. GEO builds on classic SEO authority - it does not replace it. Our [technical SEO complete guide](/blog/what-is-technical-seo-complete-guide) covers the foundation that makes AI optimization possible.

---

## The 2026 AI Search Optimization Checklist

### Technical Foundations

- **Publish an llms.txt file** at your domain root with a one-paragraph summary and links to your 10-20 most important pages.
- **Add Article, FAQPage, and Organization schema** using JSON-LD so machines get verified facts, not guesses. See our [schema markup guide](/blog/what-is-schema-markup-and-how-to-add-it).
- **Keep robots.txt and sitemap.xml current**, and do not block AI crawlers (GPTBot, Google-Extended, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot) unless you have a deliberate reason.
- **Serve clean, fast HTML** - AI crawlers parse server-rendered content far more reliably than JavaScript-dependent pages.

### Content Foundations

- **Lead with a direct answer** - a 40-60 word summary answering the primary question in the first screen of every article.
- **Cite named sources for statistics** - "BrightLocal, 2025" beats "studies show."
- **Write quotable definitions** - one crisp sentence defining each key term.
- **Build FAQ sections** that mirror how people actually ask questions in conversational AI.
- **Cover topics with genuine depth** - shallow 500-word pages are never cited; comprehensive, original analysis is.

### Authority Foundations

- **Earn third-party mentions** - digital PR, podcast appearances, and industry directories feed AI training and retrieval data.
- **Keep brand facts consistent** across your website, social profiles, and directories so AI systems do not find contradictions.
- **Monitor AI visibility** - regularly ask ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity what they say about your brand and category, and fix the gaps you find.

---

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Does llms.txt guarantee my site will be cited by ChatGPT?

No. llms.txt is an emerging convention, not an enforced standard, and no file can force an AI model to cite you. It removes friction for the crawlers that do read it and signals that your site is maintained for machine readability. Citation depends on content quality, topical authority, and relevance to the user's query - the file is one input among many.

### Is GEO replacing traditional SEO?

No - it extends it. Everything that makes AI optimization work (fast crawlable pages, structured data, authoritative backlinks, genuine expertise) is also classic SEO. Businesses that skip technical SEO fundamentals and chase AI tricks alone consistently underperform. Think of GEO as SEO's next chapter, not its replacement.

### How long does it take to see results from AI search optimization?

Typically 2-4 months for measurable citation improvements, since AI systems refresh their indexes and training data on their own schedules. The fastest wins usually come from FAQ-structured content and schema markup on pages that already rank in traditional search.

### Should small businesses in Bangladesh care about AI search?

Yes - arguably more than anyone. With nearly half of US consumers already asking AI tools for local business recommendations (BrightLocal, 2026), and Bangladeshi consumers adopting AI assistants rapidly, being the business the AI recommends is becoming a genuine competitive moat. The cost of a well-structured llms.txt and FAQ content is minimal compared to paid advertising.

### Can ArtX implement llms.txt and GEO for my website?

Yes. Our [SEO services](/services/seo-services) include AI search readiness audits: llms.txt creation, schema implementation, content restructuring for citation, and ongoing AI-visibility monitoring. [Contact our team](/contact) for an assessment of your current AI visibility.

---

# Google Business Profile Optimization in Bangladesh: Rank in the Local Pack (2026)

When someone in Gulshan searches "best dental clinic near me," Google shows a map with three businesses before any organic result. That local 3-pack captures the overwhelming majority of clicks and calls - and the businesses inside it got there largely because of their Google Business Profile (GBP).

The data is unambiguous. In 2025, 97% of consumers read online reviews for local businesses (BrightLocal, 2025), 73% of local searches start on a mobile device, and Google confirms that businesses with complete profiles are considered 2.7x more reputable, get 70% more visits, and are 50% more likely to make a sale. Yet just 35% of small businesses have even claimed their profile - meaning most of your competitors are invisible where it matters most.

This guide walks through exactly how to optimize your Google Business Profile for the Bangladeshi market, step by step.

---

## Quick Answer: How Do I Rank Higher on Google Maps in Bangladesh?

> **The Short Answer:** To rank in Google's local 3-pack in Bangladesh, claim and fully complete your Google Business Profile, choose the most accurate primary category, keep your name-address-phone consistent everywhere, collect a steady stream of genuine Google reviews and reply to every one, add 50+ real photos of your business, post weekly updates, and keep your hours (including Eid and holiday hours) perfectly accurate. Reviews, categories, and proximity are the three heaviest local ranking factors.

For the full ranking-factor picture, see our breakdown of [local SEO ranking factors in Dhaka](/blog/local-seo-ranking-factors-dhaka).

---

## Why Google Business Profile Matters More Than Your Website for Local Searches

Your website is essential - but for "near me" queries, your GBP is the storefront. Consider the funnel: 46% of all Google searches carry local intent, 84% of consumers searched for a local business in the past three months, and 75% decide which business to use in under 30 minutes (BrightLocal, 2025-2026). They are not browsing - they are choosing.

Google's own data shows customers are 70% more likely to visit and 50% more likely to buy from businesses with complete profiles. In Dhaka's dense commercial districts - Banani, Dhanmondi, Uttara, Mirpur - the difference between position 1 and position 4 in the local pack is often the difference between a ringing phone and silence.

### Bangladesh-Specific Local Search Realities

- **Mobile-first behavior:** With 119.29 million mobile internet users in Bangladesh (BTRC, June 2025), virtually every local search happens on a phone, often on the move. Your profile must be flawless on mobile.
- **Bilingual search:** Customers search in both English ("best restaurant Dhanmondi") and Bangla. Your profile should serve both - see our [multilingual website SEO guide](/blog/multilingual-website-seo-bangladesh) for the website side.
- **Landmark navigation:** Addresses like "House 12, Road 5, Banani DOHS" work far better than street names alone. Include landmarks in your business description.

---

## Step-by-Step Google Business Profile Optimization

### 1. Claim, Verify, and Choose the Right Category

Visit business.google.com, claim your listing, and complete verification (usually via video or postcard in Bangladesh). Then choose the single most accurate **primary category** - this is the #1 individual local-pack ranking factor (Whitespark Local Search Ranking Factors, 2026), ahead of proximity and keywords in the GBP business title. Add every relevant secondary category, but never stuff keywords into your business name: "ArtX Dev" beats a keyword-stuffed name, and stuffing risks suspension.

### 2. Complete Every Single Field

Incomplete profiles lose. Google's data shows complete profiles get 7x more clicks than incomplete ones. Fill in:

- Accurate business name, address, and phone (matching your website exactly)
- Website URL and appointment/booking links
- Precise service areas (e.g., "Dhaka Division" for service-area businesses)
- Opening hours, including special hours for Eid, Puja, and public holidays
- A 750-word business description using natural keywords (profiles with longer descriptions earn roughly 2.5x more impressions)
- All applicable attributes: wheelchair accessible, women-led, outdoor seating, Wi-Fi, parking

### 3. Build a Review Engine

With 97% of consumers reading reviews and only 4% saying they never read them (BrightLocal, 2025), reviews are your most persuasive asset. Businesses that start responding to reviews see their rating rise by an average of 0.12 stars and receive 12% more reviews (ReviewTrackers). Set up a system:

- **Ask every satisfied customer.** 78% of consumers were asked to leave a review in the past year, and 83% of those asked actually did (BrightLocal, 2026). A simple WhatsApp message with your review link after a completed job works.
- **Reply to every review** - positive and negative - within 48 hours. Generic templated replies put off 50% of consumers (BrightLocal, 2026); write specific, human responses.
- **Never buy reviews.** Google removed 13 million fake Business Profiles in 2025 alone; review spam leads to suspension.

### 4. Publish Photos and Weekly Posts

Profiles with 100+ photos see dramatically more engagement - businesses with extensive photo galleries get roughly 520% more calls than average (GBP data). Upload real photos: storefront, team at work, finished projects, happy customers (with permission). Then use GBP Posts weekly to announce offers, new services, and events - they expire after 7 days, so consistency matters.

### 5. Keep Information Perfectly Accurate

85% of consumers say correct contact info and opening hours matter more than price or proximity when researching a business (BrightLocal, 2025). Wrong holiday hours during Eid are the fastest way to earn one-star reviews. Update special hours at least two weeks before every major holiday.

---

## Measuring Your Local Pack Performance

| Metric | Where to find it | What good looks like |
|--------|------------------|----------------------|
| Profile views and direction requests | GBP Insights | Steady month-over-month growth |
| Phone calls from profile | GBP Insights | Track against baseline after optimization |
| Local pack position | Manual checks / rank tracker | Top 3 for primary keywords in your area |
| Review velocity and rating | GBP dashboard | 5-10 new reviews/month, 4.3+ stars |
| Photo views | GBP Insights | Exceeds competitor median in your category |

---

## Frequently Asked Questions

### How long does Google Business Profile optimization take to show results?

Most businesses see measurable movement in 4-8 weeks: review velocity and photo views improve first, local pack positions typically shift within 2-3 months as Google re-evaluates engagement signals. Brand-new profiles in competitive Dhaka neighborhoods may need 3-6 months of consistent effort.

### Can I rank in the local pack without a physical storefront?

Yes. Service-area businesses (plumbers, home services, agencies serving clients on-site) can hide their address and define service areas instead. You can still appear in the local pack for searches within those areas, though businesses with verified physical locations near the searcher hold a proximity advantage.

### What should I do about a fake or duplicate listing of my business?

Use the "Suggest an edit" flow on the duplicate, then report it through your GBP dashboard. For persistent fakes, escalate via the GBP support forum or contact support directly. Never create a second profile to compete with the fake one - duplicates confuse Google and split your reviews.

### Do I need a website if my Google Business Profile is fully optimized?

Yes. Only 40% of local businesses have a dedicated website (BrightLocal, 2025), yet 54% of diners head to a website after reading good reviews. Your GBP wins the first impression; your website closes the sale with detailed services, pricing, and trust signals. See how an [SEO-ready website](/blog/seo-ready-website-bangladesh-guide) complements your profile.

### Should reviews be in English or Bangla?

Both are fine - Google understands Bangla reviews perfectly. Encourage customers to write in whatever language feels natural; authentic Bangla reviews with local keywords can even help you surface for Bangla-language searches.

---
*Need help dominating local search in Dhaka? ArtX's [SEO services](/services/seo-services) include complete GBP setup, review-engine systems, and local citation building. [Talk to us](/contact) about your local visibility.*

title: Image Optimization for Websites: The WebP & AVIF Performance Guide (2026)
excerpt: Images are half your page weight. This image optimization guide shows how WebP & AVIF formats cut load times, improve Core Web Vitals, and lift conversions.
content: # Image Optimization for Websites: The WebP & AVIF Performance Guide (2026) Images typically account for roughly half of an average web page's total weight (HTTP Archive). That means image optimization is not a minor tweak - it is usually the single highest-leverage performance improvement a website can make. A hero image that drops from 1.2 MB to 90 KB can move your Largest Contentful Paint from "poor" to "good" in one change, and with Google confirming page experience as a ranking signal, those seconds translate directly into search positions and revenue. This guide covers modern image formats (WebP and AVIF), responsive image delivery, and the exact techniques ArtX uses to keep client sites fast. --- ## Quick Answer: How Do I Optimize Images for Website Performance? > **The Short Answer:** Convert images to modern formats - WebP for broad compatibility or AVIF for maximum compression - which are typically 25-35% smaller than JPEG at equal quality (Google Developers). Serve responsively sized images with srcset, lazy-load below-the-fold images, compress aggressively (quality 70-85), add explicit width and height attributes to prevent layout shift, and preload your hero image. This combination routinely cuts image payload by 60-80%. Before diving in, understand what you are optimizing for: our [Core Web Vitals guide](/blog/what-is-core-web-vitals-and-why-it-matters) explains the LCP, INP, and CLS thresholds your images directly affect. --- ## Why Image Optimization Matters: The Numbers - **Page weight:** Images are the largest content category on the web by bytes (HTTP Archive, Web Almanac). - **Conversion impact:** A one-second delay in mobile load time can reduce conversions by up to 20% (Google/SOASTA research, widely cited). - **Ranking signal:** Core Web Vitals - where LCP is usually an image - are confirmed Google ranking signals measured on real-user field data. - **Mobile reality:** In Bangladesh, average mobile download speeds range around 11-23 Mbps depending on the operator (OpenSignal, 2025), so a 3 MB page of unoptimized images loads painfully slowly on real connections. --- ## WebP vs AVIF vs JPEG: Choosing the Right Format | Format | Compression vs JPEG | Browser support | Best for | |--------|--------------------|-----------------|----------| | JPEG | Baseline | Universal | Legacy fallback only | | PNG | Larger than JPEG for photos | Universal | Logos, icons, transparency (or use SVG) | | WebP | ~25-35% smaller (Google) | 97%+ of browsers | Photographs, general use - the safe default | | AVIF | Up to ~50% smaller | ~93% of browsers (2026) | Maximum compression where supported | ### The Practical Strategy: AVIF with WebP Fallback Serve AVIF first, fall back to WebP, and keep JPEG only for ancient browsers. In HTML: ```html ``` Modern frameworks (Next.js Image, Nuxt Img) handle this negotiation automatically. If your site runs on one, enable automatic format serving and stop thinking about it - but verify the output, because misconfigured pipelines sometimes serve AVIF at needlessly high quality settings. --- ## The 7-Step Image Optimization Workflow ### 1. Resize to Display Size Never serve a 4000px original where 1200px displays. Generate multiple widths (e.g., 640, 1024, 1600, 2400) and let `srcset` pick. This alone often cuts 70% of bytes. ### 2. Compress Intelligently For photographs, WebP quality 70-80 and AVIF quality 50-60 are visually indistinguishable from the original for most viewers. Tools: Squoosh (browser-based), Sharp (Node.js pipeline), or cwebp/cavif CLI. Avoid double-compressing already-compressed images. ### 3. Lazy-Load Below the Fold Add `loading="lazy"` to every image not visible on initial load. This is now native browser behavior - no JavaScript library needed. Never lazy-load your LCP hero image; instead use `fetchpriority="high"` and preload it. ### 4. Set Explicit Dimensions Always include `width` and `height` attributes (or CSS aspect-ratio). Without them, images cause Cumulative Layout Shift as they load - text jumps, users mis-click, and your CLS score fails the 0.1 "good" threshold. ### 5. Use SVG for Graphics Logos, icons, and illustrations should be SVG - infinitely scalable, typically under 5 KB, and razor-sharp on retina displays. Never use PNG screenshots of text. ### 6. Serve from a CDN with Caching Images should carry long cache headers (immutable, 1 year) with fingerprinted filenames. A CDN edge node in Singapore or Mumbai serves Bangladeshi users far faster than a US origin server. ### 7. Audit Regularly Marketing teams upload unoptimized images constantly. Run Lighthouse or PageSpeed Insights quarterly and add automated checks (e.g., a CI step that fails builds when images exceed 300 KB) so performance does not silently regress. --- ## Frequently Asked Questions ### Is AVIF safe to use in 2026, or should I stick with WebP? AVIF is safe as a progressive enhancement with WebP/JPEG fallbacks via the `` element. Browser support exceeds 90%, and the compression gains (up to ~50% over JPEG) are real. Use WebP as your baseline default and AVIF where your build pipeline supports it reliably. ### Will compressing images hurt their visual quality? Not if done correctly. Modern codecs are remarkably efficient: WebP at quality 75 typically looks identical to a JPEG at quality 90 while using a third fewer bytes. Always compare visually at 100% zoom before publishing, and keep lossless masters archived for re-export. ### How do I optimize images in WordPress? Use a plugin that converts uploads to WebP/AVIF automatically (e.g., WebP Express, ShortPixel, or Imagify), enable lazy loading (built into WordPress core since 5.5), and choose a theme that declares image dimensions. Audit with PageSpeed Insights after setup. Our [WordPress development services](/services/wordpress-development) include performance tuning as standard. ### Do background images and sliders hurt performance? Almost always, yes. Full-screen background sliders are the most common LCP killer we encounter in audits. If you must use one, preload only the first slide, compress it aggressively, and consider replacing the slider with a single optimized hero image - sliders rarely improve conversions anyway. ### Can image optimization alone fix a slow website? It is usually the biggest single win, but not the whole story. Third-party scripts, unoptimized JavaScript bundles, and slow server response (TTFB) also matter. A proper [technical performance audit](/services/web-development) identifies the full picture. --- *ArtX builds performance into every project from day one - modern formats, responsive delivery, and automated checks. See [why teams choose us](/why-us) or [get a performance audit](/contact).*

title: Headless CMS Comparison 2026: Strapi vs Sanity vs Contentful (Honest Guide)
excerpt: Strapi vs Sanity vs Contentful: an honest 2026 headless CMS comparison covering pricing, developer experience, and which platform fits your project.
content:
# Headless CMS Comparison 2026: Strapi vs Sanity vs Contentful (Honest Guide)

A headless CMS separates your content management backend from the presentation frontend: editors work in a clean admin panel while developers consume content via API and render it in React, Next.js, or any framework. The result is faster websites, happier editors, and content that can feed a website, mobile app, and digital signage simultaneously.

But which headless CMS should you choose? We build with all three regularly at ArtX. Here is the honest comparison we give clients - no affiliate bias, no vendor talking points.

---

## Quick Answer: Which Headless CMS Should I Choose in 2026?

> **The Short Answer:** Choose Strapi if you want a free, self-hosted open-source CMS with full data control; choose Sanity if your editors need a real-time collaborative studio and your developers want maximum schema flexibility; choose Contentful if you are an enterprise team that values a mature ecosystem, SLAs, and marketplace apps over cost. For most small-to-medium Bangladeshi businesses, Strapi's free self-hosted tier or Sanity's generous free plan beats Contentful's pricing.

If you are coming from WordPress rather than starting fresh, read our [headless WordPress with React guide](/blog/headless-wordpress-with-react-guide) first - keeping WordPress as the headless backend is often the pragmatic middle path.

---

## What "Headless" Actually Means (60-Second Primer)

In a traditional CMS (WordPress, Drupal), the backend and the website theme are fused: content lives in a database and the same system renders the HTML. In a headless CMS, the backend only manages content and exposes it through REST or GraphQL APIs. Your frontend - built with Next.js, Astro, or similar - fetches that content and renders it independently. Benefits: dramatically faster page loads (static generation), freedom to redesign without migrating content, and one content hub feeding web, app, and IoT.

---

## Head-to-Head Comparison

| Criteria | Strapi | Sanity | Contentful |
|----------|--------|--------|------------|
| License / hosting | Open-source, self-hosted (or Strapi Cloud) | Hosted SaaS (content lake) | Hosted SaaS |
| Free tier | Fully free self-hosted | Generous free tier (datasets, bandwidth) | Limited free tier, then per-seat pricing |
| Typical cost at scale | Server cost only (self-hosted) | Usage-based, moderate | Highest of the three; enterprise plans are expensive |
| Content modeling | Visual builder, good defaults | Code-defined schemas (GROQ) - most flexible | Visual builder, mature |
| Real-time collaboration | Basic | Excellent (live multi-user editing) | Good |
| Developer experience | REST + GraphQL out of the box | GROQ query language (learning curve) | Clean APIs, huge SDK ecosystem |
| Media handling | Built-in media library | Asset pipeline with on-the-fly transforms | Strong asset management |
| Best for | Budget-conscious teams, data sovereignty | Editorial teams, structured content | Enterprises needing SLAs and marketplace apps |

---

## Deep Dive: When Each One Wins

### Strapi: The Self-Hosted Workhorse

Strapi is open-source Node.js software you run on your own server - a $6-12/month VPS handles most small business sites. You own your data completely, which matters for regulated industries and clients wary of SaaS lock-in. The admin panel is intuitive for non-technical editors, and both REST and GraphQL APIs work out of the box. Downsides: you are responsible for updates, backups, and scaling; the plugin ecosystem is smaller than Contentful's marketplace.

**Choose Strapi when:** budget matters, you need data residency control, or you already have DevOps capacity. It is our default recommendation for Bangladeshi SMEs.

### Sanity: The Editor's Favorite

Sanity's real-time collaborative studio feels like Google Docs for structured content - multiple editors work simultaneously with live cursors. Content is stored as structured data (not HTML blobs), so the same content powers your website, app, and even AI chatbots cleanly. GROQ, its query language, is powerful but takes developers a week or two to learn. The free tier is genuinely generous.

**Choose Sanity when:** you have an active editorial team, publish frequently, or need content reused across many surfaces. Media companies and content-heavy startups love it.

### Contentful: The Enterprise Standard

Contentful pioneered the headless category and it shows: the most mature API, the largest app marketplace, SOC 2 compliance, and enterprise SLAs. It is also the most expensive by a wide margin once you exceed the free tier - per-seat pricing adds up fast with large editorial teams. For funded startups and corporates where procurement prefers established vendors, it is the safe choice.

**Choose Contentful when:** you need enterprise compliance, have budget for per-seat licensing, or want the deepest third-party integration ecosystem.

---

## Migration and SEO Considerations

Going headless changes your URLs, rendering, and sitemaps - plan the migration like any [website migration](/blog/website-migration-seo-checklist): map every old URL to a new one with 301 redirects, regenerate your sitemap, and verify structured data survives the move. The performance upside is significant: statically generated headless frontends routinely score 95+ on Lighthouse, which compounds into better [Core Web Vitals](/blog/what-is-core-web-vitals-and-why-it-matters) and rankings.

---

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Is a headless CMS overkill for a small business website?

Often, yes. If you publish a few pages a month and need no mobile app, a well-built WordPress or static site is simpler and cheaper to maintain. Headless pays off when you have frequent publishing, multiple content surfaces, or strict performance requirements. We talk clients out of headless about as often as we recommend it.

### Can I keep WordPress and still go headless?

Absolutely - WordPress has a mature REST API and WPGraphQL. This "headless WordPress" approach keeps the editing experience your team knows while delivering a fast React frontend. It is the lowest-risk path to headless for existing WordPress sites.

### How much does it cost to build a headless CMS website?

At ArtX, typical headless builds range from 150,000 BDT for a focused marketing site to 800,000+ BDT for complex multi-surface platforms, plus CMS hosting costs (from nearly free for self-hosted Strapi to five figures monthly for enterprise Contentful). See our [pricing](/pricing) for current packages.

### Which headless CMS is best for SEO?

All three can be excellent for SEO because SEO depends on the frontend implementation: server-side rendering, metadata control, sitemaps, and schema markup. Sanity's structured content gives a slight edge for programmatic SEO at scale, but a poorly built Next.js frontend will outrank nothing regardless of CMS choice.

### How long does a headless migration take?

A typical marketing-site migration takes 6-10 weeks including content modeling, frontend build, redirect mapping, and QA. Enterprise migrations with multiple locales and integrations run 3-6 months. Our [enterprise web architecture guide](/blog/enterprise-web-application-architecture) covers the planning in depth.

---
*ArtX designs and builds headless websites with Strapi, Sanity, and Contentful - and we will tell you honestly when you do not need one. [Start the conversation](/contact).*

title: On-Page SEO Checklist 2026: 21 Elements Every Page Needs to Rank
excerpt: The complete on-page SEO checklist for 2026: title tags, headings, schema, internal links & Core Web Vitals. 21 elements every ranking page needs.

# On-Page SEO Checklist 2026: 21 Elements Every Page Needs to Rank

On-page SEO is everything you control directly on a web page to help it rank: the words, the HTML, the structure, and the experience. While backlinks and authority matter enormously, we regularly see pages jump 10-30 positions from on-page fixes alone - because most websites get the basics wrong.

This is the exact 21-point checklist our team runs on every page before it goes live. Work through it top to bottom.

---

## Quick Answer: What Is the On-Page SEO Checklist for 2026?

> **The Short Answer:** Every page that ranks in 2026 needs: one primary keyword in the title tag, URL, H1, and first 100 words; a compelling 50-160 character meta description; a single clear H1 with logical H2/H3 hierarchy; 1,500+ words of genuinely helpful content; descriptive image alt text; schema markup; 2-5 internal links; fast Core Web Vitals; and mobile-perfect rendering. Nail these fundamentals before chasing advanced tactics - they drive the majority of on-page ranking power.

If your pages are not ranking at all, start with our diagnostic guide on [why your website is not ranking on Google](/blog/why-your-website-is-not-ranking-on-google) - the cause is often technical rather than content-related.

---

## The 21-Point On-Page SEO Checklist

### Keyword and Intent (Points 1-4)

**1. One primary keyword per page.** Each page targets exactly one primary keyword and a tight cluster of variants. Two pages targeting the same keyword cannibalize each other.

**2. Keyword in the title tag (front-loaded).** Keep titles 50-60 characters so they do not truncate in search results, and put the primary keyword as close to the start as naturally possible.

**3. Keyword in the URL slug.** Short, descriptive, kebab-case URLs: `/on-page-seo-checklist-2026/` beats `/blog/post?id=4821`.

**4. Search intent match.** Before writing, Google the keyword and study the top 10 results. If they are all product pages and you wrote a 3,000-word guide, you will not rank - match the format searchers expect.

### Content Structure (Points 5-10)

**5. One H1 containing the keyword.** Exactly one H1 per page, closely mirroring the title tag.

**6. Logical H2/H3 hierarchy.** Use headings as an outline a stranger could follow. Never skip from H1 to H3, and never use headings for styling - that is what CSS is for.

**7. Answer the question in the first 100 words.** A 40-60 word direct answer near the top wins featured snippets, AI citations, and impatient readers alike.

**8. Comprehensive depth.** Top-ranking content averages well over 1,500 words for competitive queries - not because length itself ranks, but because thorough answers naturally cover the subtopics searchers need.

**9. Original value.** Add something the top 10 lack: original data, a worked example, a comparison table, expert quotes. Rewritten commodity content does not outrank the originals.

**10. FAQ section.** Three or more genuine questions with concise answers, marked up with FAQ schema. This is the highest-ROI on-page addition for most pages.

### HTML and Metadata (Points 11-14)

**11. Meta description that earns the click.** 50-160 characters, includes the keyword, and promises a specific benefit. It does not directly rank you, but higher CTR means more traffic at the same position.

**12. Descriptive image alt text.** Every meaningful image gets concise alt text describing the image ("team reviewing website wireframes") - not keyword stuffing. This powers image search and accessibility.

**13. Schema markup.** Add Article, FAQPage, Product, or LocalBusiness schema via JSON-LD as appropriate. See our [schema markup implementation guide](/blog/what-is-schema-markup-and-how-to-add-it).

**14. Clean, semantic HTML.** Proper `<article>`, `<nav>`, `<header>` landmarks help both screen readers and search crawlers understand page structure.

### Links and Experience (Points 15-21)

**15. 2-5 internal links.** Link to relevant pages with descriptive anchor text. Internal links distribute authority and guide crawlers - audit yours quarterly.

**16. Outbound links to authoritative sources.** Citing named sources (Google Developers, industry studies) signals well-researched content.

**17. Mobile-perfect rendering.** With mobile-first indexing, your page is judged on its mobile version. Test on a real phone, not just dev tools.

**18. Core Web Vitals pass.** LCP under 2.5s, INP under 200ms, CLS under 0.1 - measured on real-user field data. Our [Core Web Vitals guide](/blog/what-is-core-web-vitals-and-why-it-matters) shows how.

**19. HTTPS and no intrusive interstitials.** Table stakes in 2026, but we still encounter HTTP pages and full-screen popups blocking content on mobile.

**20. Freshness signals.** Update the content when facts change, and show a visible "last updated" date. Stale statistics are a quiet ranking killer.

**21. Clear next step.** Every page should guide the visitor somewhere: a contact form, a related article, a pricing page. Pages that satisfy intent completely *and* offer a path forward convert best.

---

## Common On-Page Mistakes We Fix Weekly

| Mistake | Why it hurts | Fix |
|---------|--------------|-----|
| Multiple H1s | Confuses crawlers about the page topic | One H1, keyword-inclusive |
| 300-word "service" pages | Cannot cover intent; outgunned by competitors | Expand to genuinely helpful depth |
| Stock-photo alt text left empty | Missed image traffic + accessibility failure | Write descriptive alt for every image |
| No internal links | Orphaned pages get crawled rarely, rank poorly | Add 2-5 contextual internal links |
| Title tag = brand name only | Wastes the highest-weight on-page element | Keyword-first, 50-60 chars |

---

## Frequently Asked Questions

### How many keywords should a page target?

One primary keyword plus its natural variants. Trying to rank one page for "web design," "SEO services," and "digital marketing" produces a page that ranks for none of them. Build separate, focused pages and connect them with internal links.

### Does word count directly affect rankings?

No - Google has repeatedly said word count is not a ranking factor. But comprehensive content that fully answers the query tends to be longer, earns more backlinks, and keeps readers engaged. Write until the topic is covered completely, then stop; never pad.

### How often should I update on-page SEO?

Audit your important pages quarterly and update any page whose rankings slip or whose facts go stale. Evergreen guides benefit from an annual refresh with new data and examples. Set a calendar reminder - "set and forget" is how pages decay.

### Can on-page SEO alone get me to page one?

For low-competition, long-tail keywords, often yes. For competitive commercial terms, on-page optimization is necessary but not sufficient - you will also need authoritative backlinks and genuine brand signals. Think of on-page as qualifying for the race; authority determines where you finish.

### Should I hire an agency for on-page SEO or do it myself?

This checklist covers what a competent site owner can do with a few focused days per page. Agencies add value through prioritization (which pages deserve effort), technical fixes (site speed, crawl issues), and authority building. Our [SEO services](/services/seo-services) start with a full on-page audit - [get yours](/contact).

---
*Every ArtX website ships with this checklist completed before launch - it is part of our [SEO-ready website process](/blog/seo-ready-website-bangladesh-guide), not an upsell.*

title: Homepage Copywriting That Converts: 9 Formulas That Turn Visitors Into Buyers

# Homepage Copywriting That Converts: 9 Formulas That Turn Visitors Into Buyers

You have about five seconds. Eye-tracking studies have consistently shown that visitors form an impression of a website almost instantly, and most will leave if the headline does not immediately answer three questions: *What is this? Is it for me? Why should I care?*

Most homepage copy fails because it talks about the company ("We are a leading provider of innovative solutions...") instead of the visitor's problem. This guide gives you nine battle-tested copywriting formulas, where each one belongs on your homepage, and the mistakes to avoid.

---

## Quick Answer: How Do You Write Homepage Copy That Converts?

> **The Short Answer:** High-converting homepage copy leads with a clear headline stating the outcome you deliver (not what you do), follows with a subheadline explaining how, proves it with specific numbers and social proof, addresses the visitor's main objection before they voice it, and ends every section with one clear call to action. Write at a 6th-8th grade reading level, cut every word that does not earn its place, and make the entire page scannable in under 60 seconds.

Great copy needs a great container - see how [landing page design that converts](/blog/landing-page-design-that-converts) structures these words visually.

---

## The 9 Homepage Copywriting Formulas

### 1. The Outcome Headline

**Formula:** [Desirable outcome] + [without the painful tradeoff] + [in a believable timeframe]

- Weak: "Welcome to BrightSmile Dental - Quality Care Since 2010"
- Strong: "Straighten Your Teeth Without Metal Braces - Most Patients Finish in 6 Months"

State the result the visitor wants, in their words. "Innovative solutions" is not in anyone's vocabulary; "more customers" is.

### 2. The Problem-Agitate-Solve Opener

Name the visitor's pain precisely, twist the knife gently by describing its cost, then present your solution. This is the highest-converting hero-section structure for service businesses: "Losing customers to slow competitors? Every second of load time costs you 7% of conversions. We rebuild slow websites into sub-second sales machines."

### 3. The Specificity Stack

Vague claims are invisible; specific numbers are believed. Compare:

- "We have lots of happy clients" vs. "Trusted by 340+ businesses across Bangladesh"
- "Fast websites" vs. "Average load time: 0.9 seconds"
- "Affordable pricing" vs. "Complete websites from 45,000 BDT"

Every section of your homepage should contain at least one concrete number. If you lack numbers, borrow credible third-party statistics with named sources.

### 4. The Objection Crusher

List the three reasons visitors hesitate, and answer each before they leave:

| Objection | Crusher copy |
|-----------|--------------|
| "This will be expensive" | "Transparent pricing from 45,000 BDT - see every package before you call" |
| "What if it doesn't work?" | "Every project includes a 30-day post-launch support guarantee" |
| "I don't have time for this" | "Most clients spend under 3 hours total - we handle everything else" |

### 5. The Social Proof Sandwich

Place testimonials strategically: one right under the hero (borrowed trust), a results-focused case study mid-page (proof), and review-platform ratings near the call to action (final reassurance). Use full names, companies, and photos - anonymous testimonials convert at a fraction of attributed ones.

### 6. The "How It Works" Simplifier

Three steps, maximum. "1. Tell us about your project (15-minute call). 2. We design and build (you approve at each stage). 3. You launch and grow." Complexity kills conversions; a simple process diagram outperforms three paragraphs of methodology.

### 7. The Comparison Table

"We do X" is a claim; a side-by-side table is evidence. Compare your offering against the DIY alternative and the typical agency: price, timeline, what's included, support terms. Visitors deciding between options convert faster when you make the comparison for them.

### 8. The Risk Reversal Close

End with the guarantee, not the price. "If your new website doesn't outperform your old one within 90 days, we'll work for free until it does" removes the last shred of hesitation. Specific, bold guarantees outperform vague "satisfaction guaranteed" badges.

### 9. The Single-Action Rule

Every section gets exactly one call to action, and ideally the whole page funnels to one primary action ("Get a Free Quote") with one low-friction secondary ("See Our Work"). Pages with five competing buttons convert worse than pages with one repeated button - decision fatigue is real.

---

## Homepage Copy Mistakes That Kill Conversions

- **"Welcome to our website"** - wastes the most valuable headline real estate on the internet stating the obvious.
- **Jargon and superlatives** - "synergistic, world-class, cutting-edge solutions" means nothing to anyone. Delete and replace with plain outcomes.
- **Feature lists without benefits** - "24/7 support" is a feature; "a human answers within 30 minutes, even at 2 AM" is a benefit.
- **Burying the price** - hiding pricing does not generate more calls; it generates fewer, lower-quality calls. Transparency filters in serious buyers.
- **No clear next step** - beautiful copy with no call to action is a brochure, not a salesperson.

---

## Frequently Asked Questions

### How long should homepage copy be?

As long as necessary to answer the visitor's questions, and not a word longer. Most high-converting homepages run 800-1,500 words across sections - enough for SEO and persuasion, scannable in under two minutes. If your homepage is 300 words of vague claims, it is too short; if it reads like a whitepaper, it is too long.

### Should homepage copy target SEO keywords?

Yes, but secondarily. Your homepage should naturally include your primary service + location keywords ("web design agency Dhaka"), but its main job is conversion. Deep SEO targeting belongs on dedicated service and blog pages. Never sacrifice clarity for keyword density - Google's helpful-content systems penalize exactly that tradeoff.

### How do I write copy if I'm not a writer?

Interview your five best customers and steal their words. Ask: "What problem were you trying to solve? What almost stopped you from buying? How would you describe us to a friend?" Their unpolished, specific language will outperform anything a copywriter invents. Then hire an editor to sharpen it.

### Should the homepage be in English, Bangla, or both?

For most Bangladeshi businesses targeting local customers, English headlines with Bangla supporting options (or a language toggle) perform best - English conveys professionalism while Bangla builds warmth. Our [multilingual SEO guide](/blog/multilingual-website-seo-bangladesh) covers the technical implementation.

### How often should I rewrite homepage copy?

Review it quarterly against real customer questions: if your sales team answers the same three questions every week and your homepage does not address them, rewrite. Major rewrites typically follow repositioning, new services, or a [conversion audit](/blog/conversion-rate-optimization-cro-guide) showing specific drop-off points.

---
*ArtX pairs conversion copywriting with [landing page design](/blog/landing-page-design-that-converts) engineered around it - because great words in a confusing layout still lose. [See our work](/work) or [start your project](/contact).*

title: Restaurant Website Design: 15 Must-Have Features That Fill Tables (2026)

content:
# Restaurant Website Design: 15 Must-Have Features That Fill Tables (2026)

Here is the modern diner's journey: they see your restaurant on Instagram, Google your name, read your reviews, click through to your website - and then decide in about 30 seconds whether to book. The data backs this up: 54% of diners head to a restaurant's website after reading good reviews (BrightLocal, 2025), and 67% of consumers often or always check reviews after a local search.

Yet most restaurant websites in Bangladesh are slow, menu-hostile PDFs buried three clicks deep, with no online reservation and a phone number that goes to voicemail. Every one of those failures sends a hungry customer to the competitor whose site just works.

These are the 15 features every restaurant website needs in 2026.

---

## Quick Answer: What Should a Restaurant Website Include?

> **The Short Answer:** A high-converting restaurant website needs: mobile-first design (most diners browse on phones), the full menu as readable HTML text (never PDF-only), one-tap online reservations, click-to-call phone numbers, Google Maps integration with directions, 20+ appetizing food photos, current opening hours including holidays, customer reviews, and fast loading under 2.5 seconds. These nine essentials cover 90% of what turns a hungry searcher into a booked table.

For the local-search side of the equation, pair this with our [local SEO ranking factors guide for Dhaka](/blog/local-seo-ranking-factors-dhaka) - your website and Google Business Profile win together.

---

## The 15 Must-Have Features

### Discovery and First Impression

**1. Mobile-first, thumb-friendly design.** The majority of restaurant searches happen on phones, often while the diner is already out. If your menu requires pinching and zooming, you have lost them. Test every page on a mid-range Android phone - that is your real audience in Bangladesh.

**2. Lightning-fast loading.** A hungry visitor will not wait 8 seconds. Compress food photography to WebP, lazy-load the gallery, and aim for under 2.5-second loads. See our [mobile-first web design guide](/blog/mobile-first-web-design-bangladesh) for the full playbook.

**3. Appetizing hero photography.** One stunning, professionally shot hero image of your signature dish outperforms a slideshow of ten mediocre ones. Invest in a half-day food photography shoot - it pays for itself in weeks.

### The Menu (Your Most-Visited Page)

**4. Menu as real text, not PDF.** PDF menus are slow, unsearchable, and unreadable on phones. Publish your menu as HTML text so Google can index every dish ("best kacchi in Dhanmondi" should lead to your biryani page) and diners can find it instantly.

**5. Prices on everything.** Diners who cannot see prices assume the worst and leave. Transparent pricing builds trust and filters in customers comfortable with your range.

**6. Dietary and spice indicators.** Vegetarian, vegan, halal, and spice-level markers help diners decide fast - especially groups with mixed needs. This small detail dramatically reduces pre-visit anxiety.

### Conversion: Turning Visitors into Diners

**7. One-tap online reservation.** Every extra step loses bookings. Embed a reservation widget (or a simple WhatsApp booking button, which works brilliantly in Bangladesh) directly on the homepage - never make diners hunt for how to book.

**8. Click-to-call phone number.** On mobile, your phone number must be a tappable link in the header. Many older diners and corporate bookers still prefer calling.

**9. Google Maps embed with directions.** Embed an interactive map with a "Get Directions" button. Diners navigating Dhaka traffic need one-tap navigation, not a static address.

**10. Current hours - including holidays.** Nothing earns a one-star review faster than showing up to a closed restaurant. Update Eid, Puja, and public-holiday hours at least two weeks ahead, everywhere (website, Google profile, Facebook).

### Trust and Temptation

**11. Real customer reviews.** Embed your Google reviews directly on the site. With 97% of consumers reading reviews (BrightLocal, 2025), third-party proof on your own domain is doubly persuasive.

**12. A gallery of 20+ real photos.** Interior shots, signature dishes, happy customers (with permission). Stock food photography is worse than none - diners can tell, and it erodes trust.

**13. Your story.** A short "our story" section - the chef, the recipes, the family behind it - transforms a commodity restaurant into a destination. People book stories, not menus.

### The Technical Backbone

**14. Local SEO fundamentals.** Restaurant schema markup (opening hours, menu URL, price range), a Google Business Profile linked both ways, and location pages if you have multiple branches. This is how "restaurant near me" finds you.

**15. Online ordering integration.** Whether through food-delivery app links or your own ordering system, capture the delivery demand - a massive and growing share of Dhaka's restaurant revenue. Make the ordering button impossible to miss.

---

## What a Restaurant Website Costs in Bangladesh

| Package | Typical price (BDT) | Includes |
|---------|---------------------|----------|
| Essential one-pager | 25,000-45,000 | Menu, reservations via WhatsApp, map, gallery |
| Full restaurant site | 60,000-120,000 | Online booking system, blog, SEO setup, review integration |
| Multi-branch + ordering | 150,000+ | Branch pages, custom ordering, loyalty features |

---

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Do I really need a website if I'm on a delivery app and have a Facebook page?

Yes. Delivery apps take 20-30% commission and show you next to competitors; Facebook buries your menu and hours in an unsearchable feed. Your website is the only channel you fully control - it captures direct reservations at zero commission and ranks on Google where high-intent diners search.

### Should my menu be in Bangla, English, or both?

Both, ideally. English dish names with Bangla descriptions (or a language toggle) serve Dhaka's mixed diner base best. At minimum, ensure dish names are spelled consistently everywhere - Google matches "kacchi" searches to exact menu text.

### How often should I update my restaurant website?

Update the menu the same day prices or dishes change - stale menus are the #1 restaurant website complaint. Refresh the gallery quarterly with seasonal dishes, and post about events, iftar menus, or new branches as they happen.

### Can customers book through WhatsApp instead of a booking system?

Absolutely - and in Bangladesh it often converts better than formal booking widgets. A prominent "Book on WhatsApp" button with a pre-filled message ("Hi! I'd like to book a table for 4 tonight at 8 PM") removes all friction. Just ensure someone actually replies within minutes.

### How do I get more Google reviews for my restaurant?

Ask at the perfect moment: when the bill is paid and the diner is happy. A small table tent with a QR code linking directly to your review page, plus a genuine verbal ask from staff, outperforms every digital tactic. Never offer discounts for reviews - it violates Google's policies.

# Real Estate Website Design in Bangladesh: 12 Features That Sell Property

Buying property is the largest purchase most Bangladeshis will ever make - and the journey now starts online. Buyers compare locations in Uttara vs. Purbachal, check developer reputations, scrutinize floor plans, and shortlist projects long before they pick up the phone. If your website is a static brochure with three blurry photos and a "call for price" button, you are not even in the consideration set.

Real estate websites have one job: convert anonymous browsers into qualified leads - site-visit bookings, brochure downloads, and phone inquiries. These 12 features are what separate websites that generate leads from websites that just exist.

---

## Quick Answer: What Makes a Great Real Estate Website?

> **The Short Answer:** A high-performing real estate website needs searchable property listings with filters (location, price, size), large high-quality photos and video or 3D tours for every project, downloadable floor plans and brochures, transparent pricing or clear price ranges, an instant inquiry/WhatsApp button on every listing, developer credibility content (completed projects, handover track record), and fast mobile performance. Every listing page should capture leads even from visitors not ready to call yet.

Lead capture is the entire game in property - our [B2B lead generation website guide](/blog/b2b-lead-generation-website-strategy) covers the psychology that applies equally to high-value property sales.

---

## The 12 Essential Features

### Listings That Sell

**1. Powerful search and filters.** Location, price range, apartment size, bedrooms, project status (upcoming, ongoing, ready). Buyers who cannot filter leave; buyers who can filter stay and inquire. This is the single most-used feature on any property portal.

**2. Rich media for every project.** Minimum 15-20 professional photos per project, plus video walkthroughs or 360-degree tours where budget allows. Property is visual - listings with video generate dramatically more inquiries than photo-only listings across every market studied.

**3. Floor plans and brochures as downloads.** Serious buyers study floor plans. Offer them as instant downloads in exchange for a name and phone number - this is your highest-quality lead magnet. Gate the brochure, not the basic listing.

**4. Transparent pricing.** "Call for price" kills the large majority of potential inquiries before they happen. Publish price ranges or starting prices; serious buyers will still call to negotiate, but now they call *you* instead of bouncing to a competitor who published first.

### Trust for a High-Stakes Purchase

**5. Developer track record.** Completed projects with photos, handover dates met, and customer testimonials. In a market where delayed handovers are buyers' biggest fear, proof of delivery is your strongest sales tool.

**6. Location intelligence.** Embed maps showing nearby schools, hospitals, mosques, and commute routes. For Dhaka buyers, "15 minutes from the airport via the elevated expressway" sells more effectively than any adjective.

**7. Legal transparency.** Mention RAJUK approval status, handover timelines, and payment plans clearly. Buyers researching online are doing due diligence - help them, and you become the trustworthy choice.

### Lead Capture That Never Sleeps

**8. WhatsApp inquiry on every listing.** In Bangladesh, WhatsApp is the de facto sales channel. A floating WhatsApp button with a pre-filled message ("I'm interested in the 1,450 sq ft apartment in Bashundhara") turns browsing into conversation instantly.

**9. Site-visit booking.** An embedded calendar booking form ("Book a site visit this weekend") converts far better than a generic contact form. Send automated SMS/WhatsApp confirmations to reduce no-shows.

**10. Lead magnets for early-stage buyers.** "2026 Dhaka Property Price Guide" or "Apartment Buying Checklist" as downloadable PDFs capture buyers months before they are ready - then nurture them with email or WhatsApp follow-ups until they are.

### Technical Foundations

**11. Blazing mobile performance.** Property browsing happens overwhelmingly on phones, often on slow connections. Compress those 20 listing photos to WebP, lazy-load aggressively, and keep listing pages under 2 seconds. Our [mobile-first design guide](/blog/mobile-first-web-design-bangladesh) details the approach.

**12. SEO for high-intent keywords.** Each project and location deserves its own optimized page: "3 bedroom flat for sale in Uttara Sector 11," "apartment price in Purbachal 2026." These long-tail searches carry the highest buyer intent in all of real estate marketing.

---

## What Real Estate Websites Cost in Bangladesh

| Scope | Typical investment (BDT) | Timeline |
|-------|--------------------------|----------|
| Single-project landing page | 50,000-90,000 | 3-4 weeks |
| Developer site + listings | 150,000-300,000 | 6-10 weeks |
| Full portal with CRM integration | 400,000+ | 3-5 months |

---

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Should I list exact prices or "starting from" ranges?

"Starting from" pricing is the sweet spot for most developers: it qualifies buyers on budget without locking you into a figure for every unit type. Never use "call for price" - it reads as "expensive and non-transparent" to online researchers.

### How do I handle leads that come through the website?

Speed wins: respond within 5 minutes via WhatsApp or phone. Studies across industries consistently show that lead response time is the biggest predictor of conversion - after 30 minutes, contact rates collapse. Set up instant notifications to your sales team and an automated WhatsApp acknowledgment.

### Do I need a website if I list on property portals?

Portals are rented land: you compete side-by-side with every rival, pay per lead or commission, and build the portal's brand, not yours. Your own website captures direct inquiries at zero marginal cost, ranks on Google for your project names, and presents your brand without distractions. Use portals for reach; use your website for margin.

### What about virtual tours - are they worth the cost?

For premium projects (1.5 crore BDT+), yes - 360-degree tours and video walkthroughs significantly increase inquiry quality because visitors arrive pre-sold. For mid-range projects, excellent photography plus floor plans usually suffice. Start with photos; add tours for your flagship developments.

### How do I showcase projects still under construction?

Be honest and visual: construction progress photos updated monthly, drone footage of the site, rendered 3D views clearly labeled as artist impressions, and a transparent completion timeline. Buyers accept "under construction" - what they do not accept is silence about progress.

---

title: Corporate Website vs Landing Page: Which Does Your Business Actually Need?

# Corporate Website vs Landing Page: Which Does Your Business Actually Need?

"We need a website." It sounds simple, but it hides a strategic question most businesses never ask: *what kind* of website? A full corporate website and a focused landing page are fundamentally different tools - different costs, different timelines, different jobs. Choosing wrong means either overpaying for pages nobody visits or launching a single page that cannot carry your credibility.

After building hundreds of both, here is the honest framework we use to recommend one, the other, or both.

---

## Quick Answer: Should I Get a Corporate Website or a Landing Page?

> **The Short Answer:** Choose a landing page if you have one specific goal - launching a product, running ads, or validating an idea - and need it live in 1-2 weeks on a small budget. Choose a corporate website if you need lasting credibility, organic search traffic, and room to grow: multiple services, a blog, careers, and investor relations. Most established businesses need both: a corporate site as the foundation, plus dedicated landing pages for each campaign.

---

## What Each One Is (And Isn't)

### The Corporate Website

A multi-page digital headquarters: homepage, about, services, work/portfolio, blog, careers, contact - typically 10-50+ pages. Its jobs are **credibility** (prove you are real and competent), **discoverability** (rank on Google for dozens of keywords), and **depth** (answer every question a serious buyer, partner, or recruit might ask).

- **Typical cost in Bangladesh:** 80,000-500,000+ BDT depending on scope and custom design
- **Timeline:** 6-12 weeks
- **Lifespan:** 3-5 years between major redesigns

### The Landing Page

A single, ruthlessly focused page built around one action: book a demo, buy the product, join the waitlist. No navigation menu (or a minimal one), no blog, no distractions. Its job is **conversion** - turning paid or campaign traffic into leads at the highest possible rate.

- **Typical cost in Bangladesh:** 25,000-80,000 BDT
- **Timeline:** 1-3 weeks
- **Lifespan:** tied to the campaign; often weeks to months

---

## Head-to-Head Comparison

| Factor | Corporate Website | Landing Page |
|--------|-------------------|--------------|
| Primary goal | Credibility + organic growth | Conversions from a specific campaign |
| Page count | 10-50+ | 1 (sometimes with thank-you page) |
| SEO value | High - ranks for many keywords over time | Low - single page, narrow targeting |
| Best traffic source | Organic search, referrals, direct | Paid ads, email campaigns, social |
| Navigation | Full menu | Minimal or none (reduces distraction) |
| Content depth | Comprehensive | Focused on one offer |
| Maintenance | Ongoing (blog, updates) | Minimal during campaign |
| When it wins | Long-term brand building | Product launches, ad campaigns, events |

---

## When to Choose Each: 6 Real Scenarios

### Choose a landing page when...

**1. You are running paid ads.** Sending 50,000 BDT/month of Facebook ad traffic to a generic homepage is burning money. A dedicated landing page matching the ad's message routinely doubles or triples conversion rates. This is the #1 use case.

**2. You are validating an idea.** Before investing in a full site, a landing page with a waitlist signup tests demand in two weeks for a tenth of the cost.

**3. You have a time-bound campaign.** Product launch, Eid sale, conference, webinar - a focused page with a countdown and single call to action outperforms a corporate site every time.

### Choose a corporate website when...

**4. Buyers research you before buying.** For B2B services, agencies, and high-ticket products, prospects will Google you, read your about page, check your work, and evaluate your blog. A landing page cannot carry that credibility load. See our [B2B lead generation guide](/blog/b2b-lead-generation-website-strategy).

**5. You want organic search traffic.** SEO compounds over years, but it needs pages to rank - service pages, location pages, blog articles. A single landing page captures a tiny fraction of your keyword universe. Our [SEO-ready website guide](/blog/seo-ready-website-bangladesh-guide) explains the architecture.

**6. You are hiring, fundraising, or partnering.** Candidates check careers pages, investors check traction pages, partners check credibility signals. A serious business needs a serious digital headquarters.

---

## The Smart Answer: Both, in Sequence

The highest-ROI pattern we see: build the corporate website as your foundation, then spin up dedicated landing pages for each campaign that link back to it. The corporate site builds trust and captures organic demand; the landing pages convert paid demand at maximum efficiency. They share your branding and CMS but serve different jobs.

Budget-wise, this does not mean double the cost: once the corporate site's design system exists, additional landing pages are fast and inexpensive to produce.

---

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Can a landing page rank on Google?

It can rank for its one target keyword, but a single page will never build the topical authority of a full site. Landing pages are conversion tools, not SEO assets. If organic traffic matters to you, invest in the corporate site and blog.

### How much does each cost in Bangladesh?

Landing pages typically run 25,000-80,000 BDT; corporate websites 80,000-500,000+ BDT depending on pages, custom design, and functionality. See our detailed [website cost breakdown](/blog/how-much-does-a-website-cost-in-bangladesh-2025) and [pricing page](/pricing).

### I already have a corporate website - do I still need landing pages?

If you run any paid advertising or email campaigns, yes. Your homepage speaks to everyone; a landing page speaks to one audience with one offer. The conversion lift from message-matched landing pages is one of the most reliable wins in digital marketing - our [landing page design guide](/blog/landing-page-design-that-converts) shows the anatomy.

### Can I start with a landing page and expand later?

Absolutely - and it is often the smart sequence for startups. Launch the landing page to start generating leads in weeks, then expand into a full corporate site once positioning and messaging are validated by real customer data.

### What about a one-page website - is that a landing page or corporate site?

A one-page site is a hybrid: it has the breadth of a small corporate site (about, services, contact sections) with the simplicity of a single page. It works for freelancers and very small businesses, but it caps your SEO potential since you have only one URL to rank. Treat it as a starting point, not a destination.

---

# SEO for Doctors & Clinics in Bangladesh: The Patient-Attracting Playbook

When someone in Mirpur searches "best dermatologist near me" or "root canal cost Dhaka," they are not casually browsing - they have a health concern and are choosing who to trust with their body. Healthcare is the ultimate high-trust, high-intent search category, and it is also one where Google applies its strictest quality standards.

This playbook covers exactly how clinics, chambers, diagnostic centers, and individual practitioners in Bangladesh can rank higher, appear in AI-generated answers, and convert searches into booked appointments - ethically and sustainably.

---

## Quick Answer: How Do Clinics Get More Patients from Google?

> **The Short Answer:** Clinics attract patients from Google by: (1) fully optimizing their Google Business Profile with accurate hours, services, and photos; (2) building location + specialty pages for each treatment ("dental implants Dhanmondi"); (3) publishing genuinely helpful health content written or reviewed by qualified doctors; (4) systematically collecting patient reviews and responding to all of them; and (5) displaying doctor credentials, BMDC registration, and real patient outcomes to satisfy Google's E-E-A-T quality standards for health content.

Healthcare queries also see some of the highest AI Overview penetration of any category - so structure your content for AI citation too, using our [AI search optimization guide](/blog/llms-txt-ai-search-optimization-guide).

---

## Why Healthcare SEO Is Different: YMYL and E-E-A-T

Google classifies health content as "Your Money or Your Life" (YMYL) - pages that can affect a person's health, finances, or safety. For YMYL topics, Google's quality raters apply **E-E-A-T** standards aggressively:

- **Experience:** Content reflects real clinical practice, not rewritten generic advice.
- **Expertise:** Medical content is written or reviewed by qualified professionals.
- **Authoritativeness:** The clinic/doctor is recognized - credentials, affiliations, citations.
- **Trustworthiness:** Transparent about qualifications, pricing, limitations, and privacy.

Practical implications: every health article needs a named doctor author with credentials, a "medically reviewed by" line with date, and zero exaggerated claims ("guaranteed painless" will hurt you). This is not optional polish - it is the price of admission for ranking health content.

---

## The 8-Pillar Healthcare SEO Strategy

### 1. Google Business Profile: Your Digital Reception Desk

For "near me" health searches, the local pack decides everything. Claim your profile, select precise categories ("Dental Clinic" not just "Clinic"), list every service, upload photos of the facility (clean, modern interiors build enormous trust), and keep hours - including Friday and holiday schedules - perfectly accurate. Our full [Google Business Profile optimization guide](/blog/google-business-profile-optimization-bangladesh) walks through each step.

### 2. Specialty + Location Pages

Build one dedicated page per specialty per location: "Orthodontics in Uttara," "Skin Treatment in Dhanmondi." Each page needs: the doctor's profile and credentials, treatment details in plain language, transparent pricing or ranges, before/after results (with consent), FAQs, and a prominent booking button. These pages capture the highest-intent searches in healthcare.

### 3. Doctor Profile Pages That Build Trust

Patients choose doctors, not clinics. Each practitioner gets a rich profile: photo, qualifications (MBBS, FCPS, etc.), BMDC registration number, specializations, years of experience, languages spoken, and patient reviews. These pages often outrank the clinic homepage for doctor-name searches - make them excellent.

### 4. Helpful Health Content (Done Right)

"What causes migraine?", "How much does LASIK cost in Bangladesh?", "Is teeth whitening safe?" - symptom and treatment questions drive massive search volume. Publish genuinely helpful articles authored by your doctors, reviewed annually, with clear "consult a doctor" guidance. Never diagnose definitively online; educate and invite consultation. This content also feeds AI answers - healthcare is among the top categories for AI Overview appearances.

### 5. Review Generation System

With 97% of consumers reading reviews (BrightLocal, 2025), your rating is your reputation. Ask satisfied patients at checkout via a QR code to your Google review page, respond to every review professionally (never disclose patient details in replies - privacy law and ethics demand it), and address negative reviews with empathy and an invitation to resolve offline.

### 6. Technical Health: Speed, Mobile, Accessibility

Patients often search in distress on phones. Your site must load in under 2.5 seconds, offer one-tap calling and WhatsApp booking, and meet accessibility basics (readable fonts, sufficient contrast) for elderly patients. See our [website accessibility checklist](/blog/website-accessibility-checklist-bangladesh).

### 7. Multilingual Content

Patients search in both English ("best cardiologist Dhaka") and Bangla. Serve both with properly implemented hreflang - our [multilingual SEO guide](/blog/multilingual-website-seo-bangladesh) covers the technical setup.

### 8. Appointment Booking Without Friction

Every page needs an unmissable booking path: online form, WhatsApp button, and click-to-call. Reduce form fields to the minimum (name, phone, preferred time) - every extra field loses patients. Confirm bookings instantly via SMS/WhatsApp to cut no-shows.

---

## What Healthcare SEO Costs in Bangladesh

| Engagement | Typical monthly (BDT) | Suitable for |
|------------|----------------------|--------------|
| Local SEO essentials | 20,000-40,000 | Single-chamber practitioners |
| Full clinic SEO | 50,000-100,000 | Multi-doctor clinics, diagnostic centers |
| Hospital-grade program | 120,000+ | Hospitals, chains with content teams |

Expect 4-6 months for significant movement in competitive Dhaka specialties; less competitive niches and locations move faster.

---

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Is it ethical to do SEO for medical services?

Yes - when done honestly. SEO simply makes qualified, ethical providers findable. The line is clear: educate truthfully, display real credentials, never guarantee outcomes, and never publish misleading before/after content. Google's guidelines and medical advertising ethics align here.

### Can a clinic rank without a big advertising budget?

Absolutely. Local healthcare SEO is one of the highest-ROI channels precisely because intent is so strong - a single implant or LASIK patient can be worth 50,000-150,000 BDT. Consistent GBP optimization, reviews, and helpful content outperform paid ads on cost-per-acquisition within 6-12 months for most clinics.

### How do I handle negative patient reviews?

Respond publicly within 24-48 hours with empathy, without discussing the patient's case ("We're sorry to hear about your experience; please contact us directly so we can help"). Then resolve privately. A thoughtful response to a negative review often impresses prospective patients more than a page of five-star reviews.

### Should doctors be on social media for SEO?

Social signals do not directly rank your site, but active, professional social profiles build the brand searches and reviews that do. Short health-education videos perform exceptionally well in Bangladesh - repurpose them as website content for double value.

### Do I need separate websites for each branch?

No - one strong website with dedicated location pages per branch is far better for SEO than splitting authority across multiple domains. Each branch gets its own Google Business Profile pointing to its location page. Our [local SEO guide](/blog/local-seo-ranking-factors-dhaka) details the structure.

---
