# SEO Pricing in Bangladesh 2026: What Agencies Charge & What's Worth Paying For

"How much does SEO cost?" is the first question every business asks and the hardest to answer honestly - because SEO pricing in Bangladesh ranges from 15,000 BDT/month freelancers to 200,000+ BDT/month full-service engagements, and the difference is not just price. It is scope, expertise, and whether anything actually happens.

This guide breaks down real market pricing, what each tier includes, the pricing models agencies use, and how to tell a genuine SEO partner from an expensive disappointment - including the red flags we wish every buyer knew.

---

## Quick Answer: How Much Does SEO Cost in Bangladesh in 2026?

> **The Short Answer:** In 2026, SEO in Bangladesh typically costs: 15,000-35,000 BDT/month for freelancer or basic local SEO; 40,000-90,000 BDT/month for professional agency retainers covering technical, on-page, and content; and 100,000-200,000+ BDT/month for competitive national campaigns or e-commerce SEO. One-time SEO audits run 25,000-75,000 BDT. Be deeply skeptical of anyone promising page-one rankings in 30 days at any price - and of prices so low the work cannot possibly be real.

For the website side of the investment, see our [website cost guide](/blog/how-much-does-a-website-cost-in-bangladesh-2025); for keeping either healthy, our [maintenance cost breakdown](/blog/website-maintenance-cost-and-checklist).

---

## SEO Pricing Models Explained

### Monthly Retainer (Most Common)

You pay a fixed monthly fee for ongoing work: technical monitoring, content creation, link building, and reporting. Best for businesses committed to 6+ months of growth. This is the model behind nearly all serious SEO results - rankings compound with consistent effort.

### Project-Based

A fixed fee for defined scope: a technical audit, a site migration, or a 10-page content build-out. Typical range: 50,000-300,000 BDT depending on scope. Best when you have an in-house team to maintain momentum afterward.

### Hourly Consulting

3,000-10,000 BDT/hour for senior strategists. Best for audits, second opinions, and training your team. Avoid hourly for ongoing execution - incentives misalign.

### Performance-Based ("Pay Per Ranking")

We advise against this model. It incentivizes agencies to target easy, worthless keywords that rank quickly but drive zero revenue - while your real keywords stagnate.

---

## What Each Price Tier Actually Buys

| Monthly budget | What you realistically get | Best for |
|----------------|---------------------------|----------|
| 15,000-35,000 BDT | Freelancer: basic on-page fixes, a few blog posts, directory listings | Very small local businesses, startups testing SEO |
| 40,000-90,000 BDT | Agency team: technical SEO, content strategy + production, digital PR/link building, monthly reporting | SMEs serious about organic growth |
| 100,000-200,000+ BDT | Senior team: competitive national keywords, e-commerce SEO at scale, content teams, dedicated strategist | Competitive industries, e-commerce, multi-location |

### What Drives the Price Up (Legitimately)

- **Competition:** Ranking nationally costs multiples of ranking for a niche local term.
- **Content volume:** Four expert articles a month costs more than one - and usually earns more.
- **Technical debt:** A slow, broken site needs engineering hours before content can perform.
- **Link authority gap:** New domains in competitive niches need sustained digital PR.

---

## Red Flags: How to Spot Bad SEO Deals

### Guaranteed #1 rankings

No one can guarantee rankings - not even Google employees. Guarantees signal either ignorance or a plan to target keywords nobody searches. Run.

### Secret methods and no reporting

Legitimate SEO is transparent: you should see exactly what was done each month (pages optimized, content published, links earned) and how rankings, traffic, and leads moved. "Trust our proprietary system" with no reports is a scam structure.

### Suspiciously cheap at scale

10,000 BDT/month for "500 backlinks and 20 articles" means spun content and link spam - tactics that earned short-term gains in 2015 and earn penalties in 2026. Cleaning up a penalized site costs far more than doing it right initially.

### No questions about your business

If an agency quotes without asking about your margins, sales cycle, and best customers, they are selling a commodity package, not a growth strategy. SEO that does not connect to revenue is theater.

---

## How to Evaluate an SEO Proposal: 7 Questions

1. **What exactly will you do each month?** (Demand a deliverables list, not vibes.)
2. **Who does the work?** (Senior strategists or outsourced juniors? Content written by whom?)
3. **How do you report results?** (Rankings, traffic, and - critically - leads/revenue.)
4. **What happens if we cancel?** (You should keep all content, and links should be naturally earned, not rented.)
5. **Can I speak to two current clients?** (Non-negotiable.)
6. **What is your link-building method?** ("Digital PR and outreach" = good; "private blog networks" = run.)
7. **When should we expect what?** (Honest answer: technical wins in 1-2 months, meaningful traffic in 4-6, compounding after.)

---

## Frequently Asked Questions

### How long before SEO shows results?

Technical fixes can move rankings within weeks. Meaningful organic traffic growth typically takes 4-6 months, with compounding returns from month 6-12 onward. Anyone promising faster results for competitive keywords is selling shortcuts that end in penalties.

### Is cheap SEO ever worth it?

A skilled 25,000 BDT/month freelancer can be excellent for a small local business with modest goals. The danger zone is cheap *agencies* selling industrial-scale deliverables at impossible prices - the economics only work with spam tactics. Match the price to realistic labor: quality SEO is human expertise, and expertise has a floor price.

### Should I do SEO in-house or hire an agency?

In-house works when you can hire and retain a senior SEO plus content resources - realistic at 150,000+ BDT/month in total cost. Below that, an agency gives you a full team (strategist, writer, developer liaison, outreach) for less than one senior hire. Many businesses hybridize: agency for strategy and execution, in-house for content review and industry expertise.

### What's the ROI of SEO compared to Facebook ads?

Paid ads stop the day you stop paying; SEO compounds. Typical payback: ads win months 1-3, SEO pulls even around months 6-9, and SEO dominates from year two onward on cumulative ROI. The strongest businesses run both - ads for immediate demand, SEO for durable growth.

### Do I need to keep paying for SEO forever?

You can reduce intensity once established, but never to zero. Competitors keep optimizing, Google keeps changing, and content decays. Most mature businesses settle into a maintenance tier (40-60% of growth-phase spend) protecting and extending their gains - similar logic to our [website maintenance guide](/blog/website-maintenance-cost-and-checklist).

---

# JavaScript Rendering & SEO: SSR vs CSR vs SSG Explained (React Guide 2026)

"Google can render JavaScript now, so CSR is fine for SEO" - this half-truth has launched a thousand invisible websites. Yes, Googlebot runs JavaScript. But rendering is expensive for Google, so it happens in a **second wave**: Google first indexes your raw HTML, then renders the JavaScript days or even weeks later. Content that only exists after JavaScript executes can wait weeks to be indexed - and in competitive searches, weeks might as well be never.

If your site is built with React, Next.js, Vue, or similar, understanding rendering strategies is not optional. This guide explains SSR, CSR, SSG, and ISR in plain terms, shows how each affects SEO, and tells you exactly which to choose.

---

## Quick Answer: Which Rendering Method Is Best for SEO?

> **The Short Answer:** For SEO-critical pages, use Static Site Generation (SSG) or Server-Side Rendering (SSR) so Google receives complete HTML immediately - no waiting for JavaScript. Use Client-Side Rendering (CSR) only for authenticated app screens behind logins where SEO does not matter. Next.js makes this easy by letting you mix strategies per page: SSG/SSR for marketing and blog pages, CSR for dashboards. Never ship a CSR-only public marketing site and expect it to rank.

Our [technical SEO for React applications](/blog/technical-seo-react-applications) goes deeper into implementation specifics for React codebases.

---

## The Four Rendering Strategies

### CSR: Client-Side Rendering

The server sends a nearly empty HTML shell plus a JavaScript bundle; the browser builds the page. This is the default for Create React App and Vite SPAs.

- **Pros:** Rich interactivity, simple deployment, great for app-like experiences.
- **Cons (SEO):** Google sees an empty page on first crawl; content waits for the second-wave render. Social media crawlers (Facebook, LinkedIn) do not run JavaScript at all - your link previews break. Slow on poor connections.
- **Verdict:** Fine for logged-in dashboards. Terrible for public marketing pages.

### SSR: Server-Side Rendering

The server renders full HTML on every request and sends it complete; JavaScript then "hydrates" it for interactivity.

- **Pros:** Google gets complete HTML instantly. Always-fresh content. Correct social previews.
- **Cons:** Slower Time to First Byte (server does work per request), higher server costs, more complex caching.
- **Verdict:** The right choice for personalized or frequently changing SEO pages (e-commerce listings, news).

### SSG: Static Site Generation

Pages are rendered to static HTML at build time and served from a CDN.

- **Pros:** Fastest possible loads, cheapest hosting, perfect SEO - complete HTML from a global edge. The best of all worlds for content that does not change per visitor.
- **Cons:** Rebuilds needed for content updates (solved by ISR below); not suitable for highly personalized pages.
- **Verdict:** The default choice for marketing sites, blogs, and documentation. If your page *can* be static, make it static.

### ISR: Incremental Static Regeneration (Next.js)

SSG pages that rebuild in the background when content changes or after a set interval - static speed with fresh content. For most content sites, ISR is the endgame: CDN-fast pages that update without full rebuilds.

| Strategy | HTML at first crawl | Speed | Freshness | SEO suitability |
|----------|--------------------|----|-----------|-----------------|
| CSR | Empty shell | Slow on weak devices | Real-time | Poor for public pages |
| SSR | Complete | Good (TTFB cost) | Real-time | Excellent |
| SSG | Complete | Fastest | Build-time | Excellent |
| ISR | Complete | Fastest | Near real-time | Excellent |

---

## How to Check What Google Actually Sees

### 1. View Source Test

Right-click your page and select "View Page Source" (not Inspect Element). If your headline and body text are missing from the raw source, you are CSR-dependent - Google's first wave sees nothing.

### 2. Google Search Console URL Inspection

Use "Test Live URL" and view the rendered screenshot plus the HTML Google captured. Compare it against what users see - missing content here means missing from the index.

### 3. Disable JavaScript Test

Turn off JavaScript in your browser and reload. Whatever remains visible is what non-JS crawlers (and users on failing connections) experience. Your core content and navigation should survive this test.

---

## Fixing a CSR Site Without Rebuilding Everything

If you inherited a client-rendered React app that needs SEO, you have options short of a full rewrite:

- **Migrate to Next.js incrementally:** Next.js supports adopting pages one route at a time. Convert marketing and blog routes to SSG/SSR first; leave the app dashboard as CSR.
- **Prerendering services:** Tools that serve pre-rendered HTML to crawlers. A workable bandage, but a bandage - it adds infrastructure complexity and can serve stale content.
- **Dynamic rendering (use cautiously):** Google officially supports serving static HTML to bots and JS to users, but calls it a workaround, not a long-term solution. Prefer real SSR/SSG.

---

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Does Google really struggle with JavaScript in 2026?

Less than it used to, but the two-wave indexing delay is real and documented: HTML is indexed first, JavaScript rendering follows later. For time-sensitive content (news, product launches, sale pages), that delay directly costs visibility. Server-rendered HTML eliminates the problem entirely.

### Is Next.js automatically good for SEO?

Next.js *enables* good SEO but does not guarantee it. A Next.js app built entirely with client-side rendering and no metadata management is just as invisible as a CRA app. You must deliberately use SSG/SSR per page, manage metadata (titles, descriptions, canonicals, Open Graph), and verify with the tests above.

### What about Angular and Vue sites?

The same principles apply: use Nuxt (Vue) or Angular Universal for SSR, or pre-render where possible. The framework matters less than the rendering strategy - complete HTML at first crawl is the requirement regardless of stack.

### Do AI crawlers handle JavaScript better or worse than Google?

Worse, generally. AI crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot) are simpler fetchers that overwhelmingly prefer clean server-rendered HTML. If AI search visibility matters to you - and our [AI search optimization guide](/blog/llms-txt-ai-search-optimization-guide) argues it should - SSR/SSG is doubly important.

### Should my web app's dashboard use SSR too?

No - authenticated pages are not indexed anyway, so CSR is perfectly fine (and often preferable) behind a login. The rule is simple: public pages that need search traffic get SSR/SSG; private app screens get whatever delivers the best UX.

---

title: Backlink Building Strategies 2026: 10 Ways to Earn Links That Move Rankings

# Backlink Building Strategies 2026: 10 Ways to Earn Links That Move Rankings

Google has confirmed it for years and every serious correlation study agrees: backlinks remain one of the top three ranking factors, alongside content quality and relevance signals. A page with strong, relevant backlinks outranks an identical page without them - consistently, measurably, and durably.

But *how* you build links in 2026 matters more than ever. Link spam - private blog networks, paid link insertions at scale, automated directory blasts - is reliably detected and penalized. What works is earning editorial links: links that publishers place because your content deserves them. Here are the ten strategies that actually work, ranked roughly by effort-to-impact.

---

## Quick Answer: What Is the Best Way to Build Backlinks in 2026?

> **The Short Answer:** The most effective backlink strategies in 2026 are digital PR (newsworthy stories and data that journalists cite), original research and statistics (which become the cited source for an entire niche), and expert guest contributions on reputable publications. These earn editorial links - links given voluntarily because content is valuable - which are the only link type that reliably improves rankings without risking penalties. Avoid buying links or using private blog networks; both are detectable and dangerous.

If your pages are not ranking despite good content, weak authority is often the missing piece - see our diagnostic on [why websites fail to rank](/blog/why-your-website-is-not-ranking-on-google).

---

## The 10 Strategies

### Tier 1: Highest Impact

**1. Digital PR.** Create genuinely newsworthy stories - industry surveys, data analyses, expert commentary on trending topics - and pitch them to journalists. One link from a major publication outweighs a hundred directory links. This is the strategy behind most "overnight" ranking jumps you see in competitive niches.

**2. Original research and statistics.** Publish the definitive data study for your niche: "We analyzed 200,000 websites and found only 54% pass Core Web Vitals." Research gets cited for years - every citation is a backlink, and journalists actively hunt for fresh statistics. Our own articles cite named studies constantly; being the *source* of those citations is link-building on autopilot.

**3. Expert guest contributions.** Write genuinely useful articles for reputable industry publications - not thin posts stuffed with links, but real expertise. One thoughtful piece on an authoritative site beats twenty guest posts on content farms.

### Tier 2: Steady Compounders

**4. The skyscraper technique (done honestly).** Find the most-linked content for your target keyword, create something genuinely better (more current, more data, better designed), then tell everyone who linked to the original. It works when the improvement is real; it fails as a templated spam tactic.

**5. Broken link building.** Find dead links on relevant resource pages, create (or identify) a worthy replacement on your site, and suggest the swap. Webmasters appreciate it because you are fixing their site - response rates are among the highest of any outreach tactic.

**6. Journalist query platforms.** Respond to journalist requests with genuine expert quotes. It is competitive and time-intensive, but links from news domains carry exceptional authority.

**7. Resource page outreach.** Curated "best resources" pages exist in nearly every niche. If your guide is legitimately among the best available, a polite suggestion to the curator often succeeds - especially for Bangladesh-specific resources, where English-language competition is thin.

### Tier 3: Foundational (Do These Anyway)

**8. Business directories and citations.** Google Business Profile, Bing Places, industry directories, and local chambers. Individually weak, collectively essential for local SEO - and inconsistent citations actively hurt you.

**9. Supplier, partner, and client links.** Ask partners to link from their "our clients" or "partners" pages. These are natural, relevant, and absurdly underused - most businesses leave dozens of these unclaimed.

**10. Unlinked brand mentions.** Search for your brand name without a link, then politely ask for the link to be added. The publisher already thought you worth mentioning; converting the mention is often a one-email win. Set up Google Alerts to catch new mentions automatically.

---

## What NOT to Do: Link Schemes That Get Penalized

| Tactic | Why it fails in 2026 |
|--------|----------------------|
| Buying links at scale | Google's spam systems detect paid patterns; manual actions demote entire sites |
| Private blog networks (PBNs) | Footprint detection (hosting, themes, analytics IDs) has made PBNs a penalty waiting to happen |
| Automated directory/blog-comment blasts | Zero editorial value; ignored or flagged as spam |
| Link exchanges ("you link me, I link you") | Reciprocal patterns are easily detected at scale |
| Exact-match anchor text stuffing | Over-optimized anchors trigger spam filters still active today |

The common thread: anything designed to *simulate* editorial endorsement rather than *earn* it eventually fails. Google's spam-fighting has only improved with AI-assisted pattern detection.

---

## How to Measure Link-Building ROI

Track these monthly: **referring domains** (unique sites linking - the metric that correlates most with rankings), **domain authority trend** (directional, not absolute), **rankings for target keywords**, and **organic traffic and leads**. A healthy campaign adds 5-20 quality referring domains monthly for SMEs. Judge on quarters, not weeks - links compound like interest.

---

## Frequently Asked Questions

### How many backlinks do I need to rank?

There is no number - it depends on competition. A local "dentist Dhanmondi" page might rank with 10-20 quality links; a national "car insurance" page needs thousands. Analyze the top 10 results for your keyword with any SEO tool: your realistic target is matching or exceeding their referring-domain profile with *better* links, not just more.

### Do nofollow links help SEO?

Nofollow links do not pass ranking credit directly, but they drive referral traffic, build brand visibility, and create a natural-looking link profile - a site with only dofollow links looks manipulated. Pursue them for traffic and credibility; the SEO benefit is indirect but real.

### How long do backlinks take to affect rankings?

Typically 2-3 months from when Google discovers and indexes the linking page. This is why link building must run continuously alongside content - stopping outreach means your link velocity flatlines while competitors keep climbing.

### Can I build links myself or do I need an agency?

Founders can absolutely earn the first 20-30 links through digital PR, partnerships, and directories. Beyond that, systematic outreach is a full-time job - which is why agencies exist. Our [SEO services](/services/seo-services) include white-hat link acquisition with full transparency on every link earned.

### Are backlinks still important with AI search rising?

Yes - arguably more so. AI systems inherit trust signals from the web's link graph when deciding which sources to cite, and the pages AI overviews cite most tend to be pages with strong traditional authority. Links remain the web's core trust currency in both classic and AI search.

---
*ArtX earns editorial backlinks through digital PR, original research, and genuine outreach - never schemes. [See our SEO approach](/services/seo-services) or [start a conversation](/contact).*

# Google Analytics 4 Conversion Tracking Setup: Measure What Matters (2026)

Here is an uncomfortable question: of the visitors who came to your website last month, how many became customers - and which page, campaign, or keyword brought them? If you cannot answer precisely, every marketing decision you make is a guess. Businesses routinely spend lakhs on ads while their analytics track nothing but pageviews.

Google Analytics 4 (GA4) - now the only version of Google Analytics, since Universal Analytics was sunset - is built around *events*, not pageviews. That makes it more powerful and more confusing. This guide walks through a complete conversion-tracking setup: the events that matter, how to implement them, and how to turn the data into decisions.

---

## Quick Answer: How Do I Set Up Conversion Tracking in GA4?

> **The Short Answer:** In GA4, go to Admin > Events, identify the events representing business value (form submissions, phone clicks, purchases, WhatsApp clicks), then mark them as key events under Admin > Key events. Implement tracking via Google Tag Manager for flexibility: create triggers for form submissions and clicks, fire GA4 event tags, test in DebugView, then mark conversions. Connect Google Ads and Search Console for the full picture. The entire setup takes 2-4 hours for a standard business site.

Conversion data is the fuel for optimization - once tracking works, our [conversion rate optimization guide](/blog/conversion-rate-optimization-cro-guide) shows how to act on it.

---

## GA4 Fundamentals: Events, Not Pageviews

GA4 automatically collects a set of **enhanced measurement events** (page views, scrolls, outbound clicks, site search, video engagement, file downloads) with zero configuration. Everything business-critical beyond that - quote requests, bookings, purchases, phone calls - must be defined as **custom events**, then promoted to **key events** (GA4's term for conversions).

The mental model: *events* are things users do; *key events* are the things users do that make you money. A scroll is an event; a submitted contact form is a key event.

---

## Step-by-Step Setup

### Step 1: Install via Google Tag Manager (Recommended)

Skip hardcoding the GA4 snippet. Install Google Tag Manager once, then deploy GA4 through it - every future tracking change becomes a tag configuration instead of a code deployment. Create your GA4 property, copy the Measurement ID (G-XXXXXXXXXX), and configure the Google tag in GTM.

### Step 2: Verify Enhanced Measurement

In GA4 Admin > Data Streams > your stream, confirm Enhanced Measurement is on. This gives you scrolls, outbound clicks, and file downloads free - genuinely useful baseline engagement data.

### Step 3: Define Your Key Events

For most businesses, the money events are:

| Business type | Key events to track |
|---------------|---------------------|
| Lead generation | Form submit, phone click, WhatsApp click, email click |
| E-commerce | Purchase, add_to_cart, begin_checkout |
| Booking/services | Booking confirmation, callback request |
| Content/publishing | Newsletter signup, brochure download, key page scroll depth |

Name events consistently in snake_case: `generate_lead`, `phone_click`, `whatsapp_click`, `purchase`. Consistency matters when building reports later.

### Step 4: Build the Tags in GTM

For each key event: create a **trigger** (e.g., form submission on the contact form's thank-you page, or a click trigger on `tel:` links), attach a **GA4 Event tag** with your event name and useful parameters (form name, page URL, value), then test in GTM Preview mode and GA4's DebugView before publishing. One untested tag can silently corrupt months of data - always verify.

### Step 5: Mark Events as Key Events

In GA4 Admin > Key events, toggle your conversion events on. Only after this step do they appear in acquisition reports and become available as Google Ads conversion goals.

### Step 6: Connect Your Ecosystem

Link Google Ads (to optimize bidding toward real conversions, not clicks), Google Search Console (to see which queries drive converting visits), and BigQuery (free export - your insurance policy against GA4's data retention limits and sampling).

---

## The Reports That Actually Matter

Forget vanity dashboards. Check these weekly:

- **Acquisition > Traffic acquisition:** which channels drive key events (not just sessions). This tells you where to spend.
- **Engagement > Landing pages:** which pages convert visitors - and which popular pages convert nobody (your optimization hit list).
- **Funnel exploration:** build a checkout or lead-form funnel to see exactly where users drop off. A 70% drop between "form viewed" and "form submitted" screams form friction.
- **Path exploration:** what do converters do differently from non-converters? Double down on those paths.

---

## Common GA4 Setup Mistakes

- **Tracking everything as a key event.** If 25 things are "conversions," nothing is. Limit key events to genuine business outcomes (5-10 max).
- **No value assigned to leads.** Give lead events estimated values (average deal value x close rate) so reports show revenue, not just counts.
- **Ignoring consent mode.** With privacy regulations tightening, implement Google Consent Mode so GA4 models missing data rather than going blind when users decline cookies.
- **Comparing GA4 numbers to old Universal Analytics.** They measure differently (event-based vs session-based) - the numbers will not match, and that is expected.
- **Never testing.** DebugView exists for a reason. Every tag gets tested before publish, every time.

---

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Is Google Analytics 4 free?

Yes - the standard version is completely free with generous limits. GA4 360 (enterprise) exists for massive properties needing higher limits and SLAs, but fewer than 1% of businesses need it. The free BigQuery export, notably, is something Universal Analytics never offered.

### How is GA4 different from the old Universal Analytics?

Universal Analytics was session-and-pageview based with rigid hit types; GA4 is event-based and flexible - any user interaction can be an event with custom parameters. GA4 is also privacy-centric (cookieless measurement, consent mode, shorter default data retention) and built for cross-platform (web + app in one property).

### Do I need Google Tag Manager, or can I hardcode GA4?

You can hardcode, but GTM is strongly recommended: it lets marketers add and adjust tracking without developer deployments, provides version control and preview testing, and centralizes all your marketing tags (ads pixels, heatmaps) in one managed container.

### Why does my GA4 traffic not match my ad platform's numbers?

Different attribution models, different counting methods, ad blockers, consent rejections, and timezone differences all create gaps of 10-30%. This is normal. Use GA4 for directional truth and trend analysis, not penny-perfect reconciliation - and always give conversion events values so business impact stays visible.

### How long should I keep GA4 data?

Set data retention to the maximum 14 months in Admin > Data Settings, and enable the free BigQuery export for permanent raw-data storage. Future you - doing year-over-year analysis - will be grateful.

---
*Every ArtX website ships with GA4 conversion tracking configured and tested - because a website without measurement is a billboard in the desert. [Get a properly instrumented website](/contact) or explore our [web development services](/services/web-development).*

title: Progressive Web Apps: Business Benefits, Costs & When to Build One (2026)

# Progressive Web Apps: Business Benefits, Costs & When to Build One (2026)

Your customers will not download your app. The average smartphone user downloads zero new apps per month, and every install screen - app store, 100 MB download, permissions, signup - bleeds potential users. Yet businesses keep paying for native iOS and Android apps that a fraction of their audience ever installs.

Progressive Web Apps (PWAs) resolve this dilemma: websites that behave like native apps - installable to the home screen, working offline, sending push notifications - delivered through the browser with zero app-store friction. Major brands have validated the model with hard numbers. This guide covers what PWAs are, what they cost, when they make sense, and when they do not.

---

## Quick Answer: What Is a Progressive Web App and Should My Business Build One?

> **The Short Answer:** A Progressive Web App is a website enhanced with service workers and a manifest file so it installs to the home screen, works offline, and sends push notifications like a native app - with no app-store download. Build one if your users engage repeatedly (e-commerce, media, SaaS, food ordering) and you want app-like retention without native development costs, which typically run 3-4x higher. Skip it if your site is simple brochureware - a fast responsive website already does that job.

---

## What Makes an App "Progressive": The Three Technologies

**1. Service workers** - background scripts that cache assets and API responses, enabling offline functionality and instant repeat loads. This is the core magic: your PWA works in a Dhaka elevator with no signal.

**2. Web app manifest** - a JSON file declaring your app's name, icons, and display mode, which makes it installable to the home screen with your branding and a splash screen.

**3. HTTPS** - required for service workers, which is also simply correct security practice in 2026.

Add push notifications (via the Push API) and background sync, and you have 90% of what most business apps need - built with standard web technologies your team already knows.

---

## The Business Case: Real Numbers from Real Companies

These are the classic, widely cited PWA case studies - treat them as directional evidence of the pattern, not guarantees:

| Company | Result after launching PWA |
|---------|---------------------------|
| AliExpress | +104% conversion rate for new users; 2x pages per session |
| Flipkart | +70% conversions; 3x longer time on site |
| Lancome | +17% conversions; 84% faster time-to-interactive |
| Twitter Lite | +65% pages per session; -20% bounce rate |
| Starbucks | 2x daily active users; works offline for ordering |

The pattern is consistent: removing install friction + faster loads + re-engagement via push = measurably better business metrics. PWAs also typically cost 3-4x less to develop than equivalent native apps (single codebase vs. two platform teams), and updates deploy instantly with no app-store review queue.

---

## PWA vs Native App vs Responsive Website

| Factor | Responsive website | PWA | Native app |
|--------|-------------------|-----|------------|
| Install friction | None | One tap ("Add to Home Screen") | App store download |
| Offline support | No | Yes (cached) | Yes |
| Push notifications | Limited | Yes | Yes (richer on iOS) |
| Development cost | $ | $$ | $$$$ (two codebases) |
| Discoverability | Google search | Google search + installable | App store only |
| Hardware access | Limited | Good (camera, GPS, Bluetooth improving) | Full |

**The honest take:** most businesses asking for "an app" actually need a PWA - they want repeat engagement and home-screen presence, not advanced hardware features. True native is justified for hardware-intensive needs (advanced camera processing, background sensors, high-end gaming) or when app-store presence itself is the distribution strategy.

---

## The Costs: What PWAs Actually Cost to Build

Converting an existing fast website into a PWA (manifest + service worker + install prompts) is a modest increment: typically 40,000-100,000 BDT at Bangladeshi agency rates. Building a full PWA product - e-commerce with offline cart, push notification infrastructure, background sync - ranges from 200,000 to 800,000+ BDT depending on complexity. Compare that against native: separate iOS and Android builds commonly run 3-4x the PWA budget, plus ongoing dual-platform maintenance forever.

---

## When NOT to Build a PWA

Intellectual honesty requires the counter-cases:

- **Simple brochure sites** do not need offline support or push notifications. A fast responsive site is the right tool.
- **iOS limitations persist** - Apple supports PWAs but with more restrictions than Android (push notification support arrived late and remains less capable). If your audience is overwhelmingly iPhone-based and push is core to your model, factor this in.
- **App-store discoverability matters** for some categories - if your competitors win through App Store search, absence there is a strategic cost.

---

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Will a PWA rank on Google like a normal website?

Yes - a PWA *is* a website, fully crawlable and indexable, provided it uses SEO-friendly rendering (server-rendered HTML, not client-only JavaScript). Our [JavaScript rendering guide](/blog/javascript-rendering-seo-ssr-vs-csr) explains the rendering requirements that apply equally to PWAs.

### Do PWAs work on iPhones?

Yes, with caveats. iOS supports installation, offline caching, and web push notifications, though capabilities lag Android. For most business use cases - e-commerce, content, ordering - iOS PWA support is sufficient in 2026.

### How do users "install" a PWA?

On Android Chrome, an install prompt appears automatically for qualifying PWAs; on iOS, users tap Share > Add to Home Screen. Smart PWAs detect the platform and show a brief custom instruction - a tiny UX detail that dramatically lifts install rates.

### Can a PWA send push notifications?

Yes - via the Push API and Notification API, once the user grants permission. Abandoned-cart reminders, order updates, and content alerts all work. Permission strategy matters: ask after demonstrating value (e.g., after a first order), not on page load.

### How long does PWA development take?

Adding PWA capabilities to an existing well-built site: 1-3 weeks. A full PWA product build: 8-16 weeks depending on features. Our [enterprise architecture guide](/blog/enterprise-web-application-architecture) covers planning for larger builds.

---
*ArtX builds Progressive Web Apps for e-commerce, media, and SaaS clients - app-like engagement without the app-store tax. [Discuss your project](/contact).*

content:
# Website Redesign Cost & Timeline in Bangladesh: The 2026 Planning Guide

Every website has an expiry date. Design trends shift, technology evolves, your business outgrows its old positioning - and suddenly the site that won you clients in 2021 is quietly costing you deals in 2026. The question is not whether to redesign, but when, how much to invest, and how to avoid the two classic disasters: the redesign that tanks your Google rankings, and the redesign that never launches.

This guide gives you real cost ranges, realistic timelines, the step-by-step process we follow at ArtX, and the mistakes that turn redesigns into cautionary tales.

---

## Quick Answer: How Much Does a Website Redesign Cost in Bangladesh?

> **The Short Answer:** In 2026, a professional website redesign in Bangladesh costs 60,000-150,000 BDT for a small business site (10-20 pages), 150,000-400,000 BDT for a mid-size corporate or e-commerce site, and 500,000+ BDT for complex platforms with custom functionality. Timelines run 4-6 weeks, 8-12 weeks, and 3-6 months respectively. The biggest cost drivers are custom design vs. templates, content migration volume, e-commerce complexity, and integrations.

For building from scratch rather than redesigning, see our [website cost guide](/blog/how-much-does-a-website-cost-in-bangladesh-2025).

---

## 7 Signs You Need a Redesign (Not Just a Refresh)

1. **Your site is not mobile-friendly** - with mobile-first indexing and 119M+ mobile internet users in Bangladesh, this alone justifies a rebuild.
2. **Load times exceed 4 seconds** - visitors bounce, Google demotes, and no plugin will save a fundamentally bloated build.
3. **Your positioning has changed** - new services, new markets, new pricing that the old site cannot communicate.
4. **Competitors' sites embarrass yours** - buyers compare; looking a decade behind costs deals you never hear about.
5. **You cannot update it yourself** - if every text change requires a developer, the CMS has failed.
6. **Conversion rates are declining** - same traffic, fewer inquiries signals a trust and UX problem.
7. **It is not secure** - outdated platforms with known vulnerabilities are a breach waiting to happen.

If you check three or more, stop patching and start planning.

---

## Realistic Timelines by Project Size

| Project size | Pages | Timeline | Typical phases |
|--------------|-------|----------|----------------|
| Small business redesign | 10-20 | 4-6 weeks | Discovery (1 wk), design (2 wks), build (2 wks), launch (1 wk) |
| Corporate / e-commerce | 20-100 | 8-12 weeks | Discovery (2 wks), design (3-4 wks), build (4-5 wks), QA + launch (2 wks) |
| Complex platform | 100+ | 3-6 months | Phased discovery, design system, iterative builds, staged migration |

The #1 timeline killer is not development - it is **client feedback loops**. Projects where stakeholders review designs within 48 hours launch on time; projects where feedback takes three weeks do not. Assign one decision-maker before the project starts.

---

## The Redesign Process That Protects Your Rankings

A redesign without an SEO migration plan is how businesses lose 50% of their organic traffic overnight. Our process - detailed in the [website migration SEO checklist](/blog/website-migration-seo-checklist) - includes:

### Pre-Launch Essentials

- **Content and URL inventory:** crawl the entire old site; every URL gets a decision - keep, redirect (301), or intentionally retire.
- **Benchmark everything:** rankings, traffic, conversion rates, page speed. You cannot prove the redesign worked without a baseline.
- **Preserve what earns:** top-traffic pages keep their URLs and core content wherever possible; change design around them, not through them.

### Launch Week

- Deploy 301 redirects for every changed URL (test every single one).
- Submit the new sitemap in Search Console; monitor the Index Coverage report daily.
- Keep the old analytics running in parallel for two weeks to catch tracking breaks.

### Post-Launch (30-60 Days)

- Watch rankings and traffic weekly - a 10-15% temporary dip is normal; a 40% cliff means redirect or technical problems.
- Fix crawl errors, broken internal links, and any pages Google struggles to render.
- Run a conversion comparison against your pre-launch baseline.

---

## 5 Costly Redesign Mistakes

**1. Redesigning for aesthetics alone.** A prettier site with the same confusing navigation and weak copy converts no better. Redesign around buyer psychology and measured UX problems, not trends.

**2. Deleting content to "simplify."** Those 40 old blog posts may look like clutter, but if they drive 60% of your organic traffic, deleting them is revenue destruction. Simplify navigation; preserve ranking assets.

**3. Skipping the content rewrite.** New design with five-year-old copy is a new suit on the same pitch. Budget for professional copywriting - it is the highest-ROI line item in most redesigns.

**4. No analytics baseline.** Without pre-launch measurements, you will argue about whether the redesign "worked" based on feelings. Measure first.

**5. Choosing on price alone.** The cheapest quote usually means templates, no SEO migration, and no copywriting - the three things that determine whether the redesign pays for itself. A 50,000 BDT redesign that loses your rankings costs more than a 200,000 BDT one that doubles your leads.

---

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Will a redesign hurt my Google rankings?

It can - temporarily and mildly with proper migration (10-15% dip recovering in 4-8 weeks), or catastrophically without one. The difference is entirely in the migration plan: URL mapping, 301 redirects, and preserving ranking content. Never let an agency tell you "Google will figure it out."

### Should I redesign or just update my current site?

If the underlying platform is sound and the design is merely dated, a visual refresh plus content updates may suffice at half the cost. If the site is slow, insecure, uneditable, or misaligned with your positioning, incremental fixes are good money after bad - rebuild.

### How do I choose a redesign agency?

Evaluate: their own website (it is their portfolio piece), relevant portfolio work, a documented migration process, transparent pricing with itemized deliverables, and client references you can call. Our [why-us page](/why-us) shows how we present exactly this.

### What should I prepare before contacting an agency?

Your goals (leads? sales? credibility?), 3-5 competitor or inspiration sites, your brand assets, access to analytics, and a realistic budget range. The more you bring, the faster and more accurate the proposal.

### How often should a business redesign its website?

Every 3-5 years for a full redesign, with continuous smaller improvements in between (new landing pages, CRO tests, content updates). Technology, design expectations, and your business all move - a site frozen in 2021 signals a business frozen in 2021. Budget for [ongoing maintenance](/blog/website-maintenance-cost-and-checklist) to extend each redesign's life.

# A/B Testing Landing Pages: The Practical Guide to Data-Driven Conversions

"We think the green button will convert better." Every marketing team has opinions about their landing page. A/B testing replaces opinions with evidence: show half your visitors version A, half version B, and let actual behavior declare the winner. Companies that test systematically compound small wins into dramatic revenue differences - a 20% lift per quarter compounds to 2x conversions in under a year.

Yet most A/B tests fail - not because testing does not work, but because they are designed badly: tested on too little traffic, stopped too early, or testing button colors while the headline repels everyone. This guide shows how to test correctly.

---

## Quick Answer: How Do You A/B Test a Landing Page?

> **The Short Answer:** Form a hypothesis based on real user data ("visitors hesitate because pricing is unclear, so adding transparent pricing will lift conversions"), create one variant changing only that element, split traffic 50/50 using a testing tool, run until you reach statistical significance (usually 95% confidence with adequate sample size), then implement the winner and test the next hypothesis. Never test without a hypothesis, never stop tests early because you like the early results, and never test multiple changes at once.

Before testing anything, ensure your analytics are trustworthy - our [GA4 conversion tracking setup guide](/blog/google-analytics-4-conversion-tracking-setup) covers the measurement foundation testing depends on.

---

## What to Test: The Priority Order

Test in order of expected impact, not ease. Button colors are easy and nearly always irrelevant; value proposition is hard and often transformative.

### High Impact (Test First)

**1. The headline and value proposition.** Does the visitor instantly understand what you offer and why it matters? Headline tests routinely produce the largest lifts - 30-100%+ - because most headlines describe the company instead of the outcome.

**2. The offer itself.** Price presentation, guarantee terms, bonus inclusions, trial length. Changing *what* you offer beats changing how you describe it.

**3. Social proof placement and format.** Testimonials below the hero vs. near the CTA; video testimonials vs. text; specific numbers vs. vague praise. Trust is the bottleneck on most pages.

**4. Form length and fields.** Every field you remove typically lifts completion. Test ruthlessly: do you really need "company size" before the first call?

### Medium Impact

**5. Call-to-action copy.** "Get My Free Quote" vs. "Submit" - specific, benefit-oriented CTAs consistently beat generic ones.

**6. Hero image or video.** Real product/team imagery vs. stock; video vs. static. Visuals set emotional tone fast.

**7. Page length.** Long vs. short versions for the same offer - the answer varies by price point and audience sophistication, which is exactly why you test.

### Low Impact (Test Last, If Ever)

**8. Button colors, font sizes, minor layout tweaks.** These produce 1-3% changes that rarely reach significance on SME traffic. Optimize these only after the big levers are pulled.

---

## Designing a Valid Test: The 6 Rules

### 1. One hypothesis, one variable

"Adding a money-back guarantee badge near the CTA will increase conversions because our survey showed trust is the top hesitation." Change only that element. If you change the headline, image, and form simultaneously and conversions rise, you have learned nothing reusable.

### 2. Split traffic cleanly

Use a proper testing tool (VWO, Optimizely, or open-source alternatives) that randomizes visitors and persists variants per visitor. Never "test" by running version A in January and version B in February - seasonality and traffic mix invalidate everything.

### 3. Calculate sample size first

Use a sample-size calculator before launching: input your baseline conversion rate, the minimum improvement you care about, and 95% confidence. Low-traffic sites may need 4-8 weeks per test - accept it, or test bigger changes that need smaller samples to detect.

### 4. Never peek and stop early

Checking daily and stopping the moment your variant leads is the #1 way to "win" tests that are actually noise. Pre-commit to a runtime or sample size, then look. Peeking inflates false-positive rates dramatically.

### 5. Run full business cycles

Include weekends, weekdays, and any campaign fluctuations - at minimum one full week, ideally two to four. B2B pages tested only on weekends produce misleading results.

### 6. Segment the results

Overall winner is not the whole story: a variant may win on mobile but lose on desktop, or win for ad traffic but lose for organic. Segment by device and traffic source before declaring victory - you may need different variants per segment.

---

## Reading Results: Beyond "Winner"

| Outcome | What to do |
|---------|------------|
| Clear winner at 95%+ confidence | Implement, document the learning, test the next hypothesis |
| Inconclusive (no significance) | Your change did not matter enough to detect - test something bigger, not longer |
| Winner contradicts your intuition | Trust the data; update your mental model (this is where real learning happens) |
| Loser | Also valuable - you now know what *not* to do; document it |

Keep a testing log: hypothesis, variant, dates, sample size, result, learning. After a year, this log becomes an institutional asset more valuable than any single test.

---

## Frequently Asked Questions

### How much traffic do I need for A/B testing?

As a rule of thumb, you need at least 1,000 conversions per month site-wide to run meaningful tests in reasonable timeframes. Below that, focus on qualitative research (user testing, surveys, heatmaps) and best-practice redesigns - formal A/B tests will take months to reach significance on tiny samples.

### What is the difference between A/B testing and multivariate testing?

A/B testing compares two (or a few) complete versions; multivariate testing combines multiple element variations simultaneously to find the best combination. Multivariate needs dramatically more traffic - it is overkill for most businesses. Master A/B first.

### Which A/B testing tool should I use?

For SMEs: VWO and Convert offer solid feature sets at reasonable prices; open-source options exist for the technically inclined. Enterprise teams use Optimizely or Adobe Target. Whatever you choose, ensure it integrates with your analytics (GA4) and does not slow your page - testing scripts are a notorious performance drag; load them carefully.

### How long should I run an A/B test?

Until you hit your pre-calculated sample size at 95% confidence, with a minimum of one full business cycle (1-2 weeks). For most SME landing pages, that means 2-6 weeks. Longer is not always better - extended tests risk contamination from external changes (campaigns, seasonality).

### My test showed no winner - was it a waste?

No. An inconclusive test tells you that element is not your bottleneck - redirect effort to bigger levers. Negative results are data: document them so nobody retests the same dead end in six months. The only wasted test is an invalid one you act on anyway.

---

# AI Content Writing & SEO: Best Practices for Ranking in 2026 (Honest Guide)

"Can AI-written content rank on Google?" - the most-asked SEO question of the last three years, and the answer is genuinely nuanced: **yes, AI-assisted content ranks every day; and yes, mass-produced AI spam gets crushed.** Both statements are true because Google does not evaluate *who* wrote content - it evaluates whether the content is helpful, accurate, and original.

The dividing line is not "AI vs. human." It is "commodity vs. value." This guide gives you the honest 2026 playbook: where AI genuinely helps content production, where it actively hurts, and the workflow our team uses to publish AI-assisted articles that rank, get cited, and convert.

---

## Quick Answer: Does AI-Generated Content Hurt SEO?

> **The Short Answer:** Google has stated explicitly that it does not penalize AI-generated content as such - it rewards helpful, reliable, people-first content regardless of how it was produced. AI content fails when it is generic, inaccurate, or adds nothing beyond what already ranks (which describes most fully automated output). It succeeds when experts direct it: using AI for research, drafting, and editing while humans contribute original data, real experience, fact-checking, and editorial judgment. The workflow matters more than the tool.

This connects directly to AI search visibility too - well-structured, factual AI-assisted content is exactly what gets cited by ChatGPT and AI Overviews. See our [AI search optimization guide](/blog/llms-txt-ai-search-optimization-guide).

---

## Where AI Genuinely Helps Content Production

### Research and Briefing

AI excels at the grunt work: summarizing the top 20 ranking articles, extracting common subtopics and questions, identifying content gaps competitors missed, and clustering keywords by intent. A research phase that took a strategist two days now takes two hours - with better coverage.

### First Drafts from Detailed Briefs

Given a thorough brief (target keyword, intent analysis, required sections, key points, brand voice examples), AI produces a solid structural draft in minutes. The key phrase is *detailed brief* - vague prompts produce vague articles. Poor input produces poor output, doubly so here.

### Editing, Repurposing, and Localization

Tightening verbose drafts, generating meta descriptions, creating social-media adaptations, and producing first-pass Bangla translations of English articles are all high-value, low-risk AI tasks. Our [multilingual SEO guide](/blog/multilingual-website-seo-bangladesh) covers the technical side of publishing both.

### Scaling Programmatic Content

For template-driven pages (location pages, product descriptions, glossary entries), AI plus structured data plus human review is the only economically viable path at scale. The template and data quality determine success - AI is the engine, not the driver.

---

## Where AI Actively Hurts (The Failure Modes)

**1. Fabricated facts and statistics.** AI models confidently invent statistics, quotes, and citations. Publishing unverified AI "research" is how brands end up citing studies that do not exist - a credibility catastrophe when discovered. Every factual claim needs human verification against a real source.

**2. Generic commodity content.** Ask AI for "tips for better web design" with no brief and you get the same 500 words as everyone else's AI output. Google's helpful-content systems specifically target content that adds no original value - and readers bounce from it in seconds.

**3. No lived experience.** AI cannot tell you what actually happened when a 400-page site was migrated, or which headline test won last quarter. Google's E-E-A-T framework explicitly values first-hand experience - the one ingredient AI cannot synthesize.

**4. Brand voice erosion.** Unedited AI output sounds like unedited AI output: competent, bland, and identical to competitors using the same tools. In crowded markets, distinctive voice is a competitive moat - do not outsource it.

**5. Factual staleness.** Models have knowledge cutoffs. An AI draft may confidently cite 2023 pricing, discontinued tools, or repealed regulations. Time-sensitive claims need current-source verification, always.

---

## The Workflow That Actually Works: AI + Expert in the Loop

This is the production process behind high-performing AI-assisted content:

| Stage | Owner | What happens |
|-------|-------|--------------|
| 1. Strategy and brief | Human expert | Keyword, intent, angle, required original insights, outline |
| 2. Research synthesis | AI (+ human review) | Competitor analysis, question mining, gap identification |
| 3. First draft | AI | Draft from the detailed brief, not from a one-line prompt |
| 4. Expertise injection | Human expert | Original data, case examples, contrarian takes, real anecdotes |
| 5. Fact-check | Human | Every statistic, quote, and claim verified against named sources |
| 6. Edit for voice | Human editor | Brand voice, rhythm, cutting fluff, headline craft |
| 7. SEO and structure pass | Human (+ AI assist) | Headings, schema, internal links, FAQ, [on-page checklist](/blog/on-page-seo-checklist-2026) |
| 8. Publish and monitor | Human | Track rankings, engagement, and AI citations; iterate |

Notice the pattern: AI handles speed and scale; humans handle truth and distinctiveness. Content produced this way is genuinely *better* than purely human content produced under the same deadline - because the research is broader and the expert's time goes to judgment, not typing.

---

## Google's Actual Position (What They Really Said)

Google's Search Central guidance is unambiguous on the principle: their focus is on the *helpfulness* of content, not its production method. Using automation - including AI - to generate content with the primary purpose of manipulating ranking in search results is a violation of spam policies. The operative phrase is *primary purpose of manipulating ranking*. Content created to genuinely help users, with AI as a production tool under expert direction, is explicitly fine. Mass-published, unreviewed AI spam is explicitly not.

---

## Frequently Asked Questions

### How can Google tell if content is AI-written?

It does not need to detect AI specifically - it detects the *symptoms* of low-effort content: no original information, no evidence of experience, factual errors, and engagement signals (bounces, no backlinks, no brand searches) that reveal readers found nothing valuable. Well-made AI-assisted content shows none of these symptoms.

### Should I disclose AI use in my content?

For standard marketing content, disclosure is optional and uncommon. For YMYL topics (health, finance, legal), transparency about authorship and expert review matters more than the tool used - a "reviewed by" line from a qualified professional carries the weight. When in doubt, disclose review processes rather than tools.

### Can small teams compete with big publishers using AI?

This is AI's great equalizer: a two-person team with deep expertise and a good AI workflow can now produce research-backed content at a pace that previously required a newsroom. The advantage goes to expertise + workflow, not headcount. Niche authority is more achievable than ever - which is exactly why starting now matters.

### How much human editing does AI content need?

Plan for 40-60% of the time a fully human article would take: the AI saves drafting time, but briefing, expertise injection, fact-checking, and voice editing are non-negotiable. Anyone promising "fully automated" publishing is selling the spam pipeline Google penalizes. Budget real expert hours or do not bother.

### Will AI search engines cite AI-assisted content?

Yes - AI answer engines cite based on clarity, factuality, and structure, not authorship method. Ironically, well-structured AI-assisted content (clear headings, direct answers, FAQ sections, named sources) is *ideal* input for AI citation. The same quality bar serves both classic SEO and GEO.

---
